title: PM chairs 54th PRAGATI Meeting
subtitle:
PM reviews infrastructure projects worth over ₹16,000 crore across 31 States and UTs

PM calls for faster redevelopment of major railway stations as multimodal transport hubs

PM emphasizes the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs

PM asks Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to improve welfare delivery

PM says focus should be on outcomes rather than on outlays to improve citizens’ lives

PM calls for linking Ekta malls with tourism and local businesses
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 9:10PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes.
During the meeting, Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks covering 31 States/ UTs and costing more than 16 thousand crores. These projects, pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, were reviewed with a focus on timelines, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution.
Prime Minister underlined that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He called for linking the malls with tourism and local businesses, noting that increased demand could create employment in rural production, packaging, storage and transportation. He stressed on review of progress regularly by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls.
Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Prime Minister stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance.
Prime Minister asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, he highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty.
During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, PM called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks.
Prime Minister asked  the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule.

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER EMPHASISES THE NEED FOR MUTUAL RESPECT EVEN AMID DIFFERENCES OF OPINION IN A DEMOCRACY
subtitle:
SANT KABIR'S TEACHINGS OF COMPASSION, EQUALITY AND SOCIAL HARMONY REMAIN RELEVANT EVEN AFTER SIX CENTURIES: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS FOR INTROSPECTION AND RESTRAINT IN SPEECH AND ETHICAL CONDUCT

PEOPLE ARE REMEMBERED NOT FOR THEIR POSITIONS BUT FOR THEIR DEEDS AND CONTRIBUTIONS TO SOCIETY: LOK SABHA SPEAKER

LOK SABHA SPEAKER HAILS SANT KABIR'S ROLE IN CHALLENGING SOCIAL EVILS AND BREAKING DOWN BARRIERS OF CASTE AND RELIGION
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla today emphasised that differences of opinion and perspective are natural in a democracy, but disagreements must always be expressed with mutual respect and dignity. He observed that Sant Kabir's teachings underscore the importance of restraint in speech, ethical conduct and respect for others, even when opinions differ.
Addressing the Sant Kabir Mahotsav and the foundation stone-laying ceremony of the Kabir Smriti Bhawan at Kabirdham Ashram in Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, Shri Birla said that Sant Kabir's timeless message of compassion, equality and social harmony continues to guide society even after six centuries. He observed that wider dissemination of Sant Kabir's teachings would foster sensitivity, mutual understanding and social harmony.
Recalling Sant Kabir's remarkable contribution to social reforms, Shri Birla said that, at a time when society was divided by caste distinctions, religious differences and social prejudices, Sant Kabir challenged prevailing orthodoxies and worked to break down divisive barriers. Through his simple yet profound couplets, composed in the language of the common people, he conveyed universal messages of truth, morality, equality and righteous conduct. Shri Birla observed that the enduring relevance of these teachings demonstrates their extraordinary power to inspire positive social transformation across generations.
Highlighting the importance of introspection, Shri Birla referred to Sant Kabir's celebrated couplet: "बुरा जो देखन मैं चला, बुरा न मिलिया कोय; जो दिल खोजा आपना, मुझसे बुरा न कोय।" He observed that, instead of finding faults in others, individuals should reflect on their own conduct and shortcomings. Such introspection, he said, fosters wisdom and humility and encourages a more compassionate approach towards fellow human beings.
Shri Birla further observed that an individual's true legacy is determined not by their position or status, but by their actions and contributions to society. Referring to Sant Kabir's simple life and enduring influence, he said that his noble deeds, selfless service and a commitment to the welfare of others leave a lasting impression on society.
Speaking about the significance of the Kabir Smriti Bhawan, Shri Birla expressed confidence that the institution would disseminate Sant Kabir's message among the people and inspire future generations to embrace his ideals. He underscored the need to take Sant Kabir's spiritual wisdom, people-centric outlook and rational expression to every section of society.
On the occasion, Shri Birla paid his respects to Sant Asang Dev Ji Maharaj and appreciated his lifelong dedication to social service and the dissemination of Sant Kabir's teachings across India and beyond. He observed that the lives of saints, marked by sacrifice, discipline and selfless dedication, provide spiritual strength and inspiration to society. He also acknowledged the contributions of saints and followers who have devoted their lives to carrying forward Sant Kabir's message.
Shri Birla called upon everyone to draw inspiration from Sant Kabir's teachings, practise restraint in speech, cultivate the habit of self-reflection and work towards bringing about positive change in the lives of others.
Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya, Sant Asang Dev Ji Maharaj, several public representatives, saints and a large number of followers of Sant Kabir were present on the occasion.
लखीमपुर खीरी, उत्तर प्रदेश में आयोजित संत कबीर महोत्सव एवं कबीर स्मृति भवन के भूमि पूजन एवं शिलान्यास समारोह में सम्मिलित हुआ।

संत कबीर की वाणी भारतीय संत परंपरा की वह अमूल्य धरोहर है, जो सदियों से मानवता को सत्य, प्रेम, समरसता और आत्मचिंतन का मार्ग दिखाती आई है। उनके विचार सामाजिक रूढ़ियों से ऊपर उठकर मानवीय मूल्यों, सदाचार और पारस्परिक सम्मान को जीवन का आधार बनाने की प्रेरणा देते हैं।

पूज्य संत श्री असंग देव जी महाराज के जन्मोत्सव के पावन अवसर पर उन्हें हार्दिक शुभकामनाएँ। कबीर धाम के माध्यम से संत कबीर के विचारों को जन-जन तक पहुँचाने का उनका सतत प्रयास समाज को आध्यात्मिक चेतना और नैतिक मूल्यों से जोड़ने की दिशा में सराहनीय है।

title: Vice-President of India and Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Meets Delegation of European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs (AFET)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 7:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President and Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today met a delegation from the European Parliament’s Committee on Foreign Affairs (AFET) led by H.E. Mr. David McAllister at Parliament House, New Delhi. He said that India-EU relations have witnessed remarkable progress in recent years across a range of sectors and thanked the leadership of both India and EU for taking it forward.
Emphasizing the shared foundation of the relationship, Shri Radhakrishnan noted that as the two largest democracies and open market economies, with diverse and pluralistic societies, India and the European Union share a common interest in shaping a resilient multipolar global order. He highlighted that institutional linkages established since the visit of the College of Commissioners in 2025, led by H.E. President Ursula von der Leyen with a whole-of-government approach, have yielded fruitful results.
Recalling high-level engagements, the Chairman mentioned that the President of the European Council and the President of the European Commission attended as Guests of Honour during the Republic Day celebrations. Their state visit for the 16th India-EU Summit provided tremendous momentum to the partnership.
Focusing on trade and investment, Shri Radhakrishnan highlighted that India and the European Union together represent a combined market of around USD 25 trillion and nearly two billion people. Terming the the proposed Free Trade Agreement as ‘Mother of all deals’,  the   Chairman expressed hope that it would be signed this year and sought the requisite support of the European Parliament in its fruition.
Addressing cooperation in technology, research, and innovation, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan appreciated the significant role played by the India-EU Trade and Technology Council (TTC) in high-level strategic coordination. He also expressed satisfaction with the conclusion of negotiations on India’s association with the prestigious Horizon Europe programme.
During the meeting, the Chairman also expressed his deepest condolences over the tragic train accident in Spain today.
Members of Rajya Sabha Shri Sanjay Kumar Jha (President, India-Germany Parliamentary Friendship Group); Shri Surendra Singh Nagar (President, India-Poland Parliamentary Friendship Group); Shri Amar Pal Maurya (President, India-Poland Parliamentary Friendship Group); and Smt. title: Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 3:48PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS), namely, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY), a next-generation governance transformation initiative aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat. The scheme is approved for implementation from 2026-27 to 2030-31 (co-terminus with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period).
Financial implications:
The scheme outlay is Rs.7,395.55 crore, comprising a Central Share of Rs.4,869.48 crore and a State Share of Rs.2,526.07 crore.
Number of beneficiaries:
Around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. Each awareness-generation episode will reach at least 1 crore citizens.
Major impact including employment generation potential:
Support the preparation of 2.55 lakh holistic Gram Panchayat Development Plans annually on the eGramSwaraj Portal, bringing together village priorities, interventions of concerned Central and State departments, and available resources through participatory and evidence-based planning.
Reach at least 1 crore citizens in each coordinated awareness-generation exercise, using existing digital and outreach platforms, Gram Sabhas and other Panchayat forums to improve understanding of relevant Government schemes and national initiatives and encourage informed discussion of their local implications.
Strengthen governance capabilities of around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, annually, through capacity building and digital handholding to improve holistic planning, communication with citizens, resource management and progress towards locally relevant Sustainable Development Goals.
Support preparation of at least 2.55 lakh online audit plans annually and timely completion of the corresponding audits through AuditOnline. Alongside improved accounting, public disclosure, and Own Source Revenue mobilization, this will strengthen accountability for available funds and support more financially self-reliant Panchayats.
No permanent posts will be created under the scheme. However, the scheme may engage need-based contractual human resources at the State, District, and Block levels as part of the institutional mechanism to provide technical support and achieve its objectives.
States/districts covered:
The scheme will extend to all States/UTs, including institutions of rural local government (traditional local bodies) in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist.
Details:
Opportunity to take advantage of national transformational reforms at the grassroots level:
National reforms and Government initiatives undertaken over the past twelve years have created opportunities for strengthening village economies, improving public services and advancing rural development. Realizing these opportunities requires informed grassroots engagement and local planning that accounts for their implications. With the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommending around Rs.4.35 lakh crore in grants for Rural Local Bodies during 2026–27 to 2030–31, Panchayats need the capacity to bring together national priorities, Government schemes, available resources, and local aspirations. PM VGSY will support this approach through holistic planning, cross-departmental coordination, capacity building, and informed deliberations through Gram Sabhas. This will help translate national-level initiatives and enhanced financial resources into locally relevant development outcomes, furthering Viksit Bharat.
Gram Panchayats as hubs of local governance:
Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY) will place the Gram Panchayat at the center of holistic local planning and coordination of development initiatives. Panchayats will be supported to bring together village priorities, relevant Government interventions, and available resources, enabling them to serve as the fulcrum of grassroots development. The scheme will connect the Viksit Bharat vision with rural communities' needs and aspirations.
Holistic planning at Gram Panchayat level:
The scheme will bring together the planning processes of all concerned Central Ministries /Departments and State Governments on a common digital platform to collaborate to prepare a holistic Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP). This will help Panchayats and departments identify gaps, align interventions, and better use available resources, including Central Finance Commission grants. Existing departmental arrangements for delivering individual schemes will continue.
A user-friendly view of development in each Gram Panchayat:
Building on eGramSwaraj and existing e-Panchayat systems, the scheme will bring information on Government schemes, beneficiaries, benefits, community assets and available resources onto a common digital platform. This will help Panchayats identify gaps, address local needs and improve planning, coordination and monitoring.
Connecting National Priorities with Local Needs:
PM VGSY will use existing training, digital, and outreach platforms, including
PANCHAM
(an AI-enabled, multilingual, two-way communication platform in 17 Indian languages), to explain government schemes and national initiatives in simple, accessible language. Gram Sabhas and Panchayat platforms will encourage community discussions, helping connect national priorities with local needs and village development goals.
Capacity building to put the approach into practice:
Capacity building will support the effective use of digital platforms, interpretation of scheme and resource information, holistic planning and communication with citizens. It will help Panchayats translate available information and informed deliberations into locally relevant development plans and follow-up action.
Transparent and efficient utilization of available resources:
The scheme will strengthen Panchayats’ capacity to effectively utilize Finance Commission grants and other funds, mobilize Own Source Revenue (OSR), and ensure online accounting, auditing and public disclosure. This will promote transparent resource use, address local development gaps and foster accountable, self-reliant Panchayats.
Implementation strategy:
The scheme will be implemented through the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. States/UTs will submit Annual Action Plans specifying activities, priorities and requirements in accordance with the scheme’s objectives and guidelines. The designated Central Empowered Committee will appraise and approve these plans in accordance with applicable procedures and norms. The Central Government and States/UTs will undertake activities within their respective areas of responsibility, supported by coordination, technical assistance, monitoring and review. Existing institutional, capacity-building, digital, and communication systems will support implementation at the grassroots level.

title: Cabinet approves Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme for Building a Globally Competitive Sports Manufacturing Ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 3:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme with a total outlay of Rs.1,856.67 crore for the period 2026 to 2033-34. The scheme aims to promote investment, manufacturing, innovation and exports, and strengthen India's position in the global sports goods sector.
Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, the Scheme seeks to strengthen India's sports goods manufacturing base through targeted support for investment, technology adoption, research and innovation, skill development, quality certification and market development. The scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India's position in global supply chains.
Aligned with the vision of Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, the Scheme is expected to attract investment, create employment opportunities, strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities and enhance the global competitiveness of Indian sports goods.
Building Integrated Sports Goods Manufacturing Ecosystems:
The Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems through the co-location of manufacturers, suppliers, testing facilities, design and prototyping centres, and ancillary enterprises. These Zones will be developed through convergence with existing industrial infrastructure under the BHAVYA Scheme and NICDC Industrial Parks, enabling efficient manufacturing, stronger industry linkages and enhanced competitiveness across the sports goods value chain.
These zones will support the creation of integrated manufacturing facilities, strengthen industry linkages and improve operational efficiencies. These interventions are expected to facilitate investment, enhance production capacities and support the growth of a robust sports goods manufacturing base in the country.
Attracting Investments and Expanding Domestic Manufacturing:
A key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth.
Together, these interventions, backed by a combined outlay of Rs.1,130 crore, are expected to strengthen domestic manufacturing, reduce import dependence, enhance domestic value addition, catalyse significant private investment, generate employment opportunities across the value chain, and improve India's competitiveness in global markets.
Strengthening MSMEs and Existing Manufacturing Clusters:
Recognising the important role of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the sports goods sector, the Scheme places emphasis on strengthening existing manufacturing clusters and supporting the growth of smaller enterprises.
Assistance will be provided for the upgradation of existing sports goods manufacturing clusters, including the development of common facilities and shared infrastructure.
Promoting Quality and International Certification:
The Scheme recognises the importance of internationally accepted quality and performance standards in enhancing the competitiveness of Indian sports goods.
Support will be provided to manufacturers for obtaining and renewing certifications from International Sports Federations, with an outlay of Rs.105 crore.
These measures will help improve product quality, facilitate access to international markets and strengthen confidence in Indian-made sports goods.
Investing in Research, Technology and Innovation
The Scheme places special emphasis on strengthening research, design and innovation in the sports goods sector.
Support will be provided for the establishment of Centres of Excellence in premier educational and research institutions to promote research in sports equipment, material sciences, protective gear and advanced manufacturing technologies.
Research and development activities will also be encouraged through convergence with the Anusandhan National Research Foundation.
Dedicated support for start-ups, in alignment with the Startup India initiative, will foster innovation and facilitate the development, testing, validation and commercialisation of new technologies, processes and products within the sports goods manufacturing ecosystem.
Developing a Skilled Workforce for the Future:
Recognising the employment-intensive nature of the sports goods sector, the Scheme will support skill development initiatives aligned with industry requirements.
The skill development initiatives will be implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and relevant industry stakeholders to ensure alignment with evolving industry requirements.
These efforts will help meet the growing demand for skilled manpower and support the long-term development of the sports goods manufacturing sector.
Taking Indian Sports Goods to Global Markets:
The Scheme seeks to expand India's presence in international sports goods markets through dedicated branding, outreach and market development initiatives. Leveraging the Export Promotion Mission, these efforts will enhance the visibility of Indian sports goods, strengthen market access and support their greater penetration in international markets.
Supporting India's Global Sporting Ambitions:
By promoting the manufacture of high-quality and internationally certified sports goods, the Scheme will support the evolving requirements of India's sports sector and athlete development programmes. Enhanced innovation, quality infrastructure and manufacturing capacity under the Scheme will complement initiatives such as Khelo India and Fit India.
The Scheme is expected to position India as a globally competitive hub for the design, development and manufacture of sports goods. By strengthening manufacturing capabilities, promoting innovation and expanding global market access, it will create new opportunities for growth, employment and exports, while supporting India's aspiration to emerge as a leading sporting nation and advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: Cabinet approves Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS) with budgetary outlay of Rs.10,000 crore upto FY 2039-40 envisages to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply-chain resilience. The scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units.
The Scheme for Container Manufacturing was announced in the Union Budget 2026–27.
The scheme has the following major components:
Interest Subvention Assistance (ISA)
with a financial outlay of Rs.859 crore
to provide Interest subvention of 3% per annum on eligible term loans (capital loans) availed by container manufacturers for setting up of greenfield container manufacturing facilities and Brownfield expansion of existing container manufacturing capacities
Operational Expenditure Assistance (OEA)
with a financial outlay of Rs.8,891 crore
to provide financial assistance for all containers manufactured as per global shipping standards and sold by eligible container manufacturers. This would help bridge the cost gap and improve the competitiveness of domestically manufactured containers.
Testing and certification assistance
with a financial outlay of Rs.150 crore
to support setting up of common facilities such as Dynamic longitudinal impact testing etc.
Overall Impact envisaged:
Increase
annual domestic container manufacturing capacity by around ten-fold, up to 7.5 lakh TEUs.
Creates an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers.
Strengthens resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains.
Generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints.

title: Three-Day Workshop on Telugu Ayurvedic Manuscripts Transcription and Editing Concludes at CCRAS-NIIMH, Hyderabad
subtitle: 2,040 folios across 30 Telugu Ayurveda manuscripts transcribed, proofread and edited during the workshop
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 8:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A three-day workshop on ‘Telugu Ayurvedic Manuscripts Transcription and Editing’ concluded today at the auditorium of the National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Hyderabad. Organised from October 26 to 28, 2026, the workshop focused on developing specialised skills for deciphering, transcribing, analysing and critically editing ancient medical knowledge preserved in historical Telugu palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.
The workshop was organised under the guidance of Padmashree Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, and Dr Koustubha Upadhaya, Advisor (Ayu), Ministry of Ayush. It was conducted under the aegis of the Centre of Excellence in Medico-Historical Studies and Indian Medical Heritage, functioning under the Central Council for Research in Ayurvedic Sciences (CCRAS)–National Institute of Indian Medical Heritage (NIIMH), Hyderabad, Ministry of Ayush.
Designed as an initiative for capacity building and human resource development, the workshop aimed to equip researchers and scholars with specialised skills required for the systematic study and preservation of India's medical heritage.
During the inaugural session, Prof. (Vaidya) Rabinarayan Acharya, Director General, CCRAS, underscored the importance of such workshops and outlined the Council's ongoing research initiatives and projects dedicated to preserving Indian medical heritage. Dr N. Srikanth, Deputy Director General, CCRAS, emphasised the need to uncover and bring to light the immense therapeutic wisdom preserved in ancient medical palm-leaf texts.
Dr G.P. Prasad, Assistant Director In-charge, CCRAS-NIIMH, outlined the core objectives of the workshop and presented the strategic roadmap for manuscript transcription. The inaugural function was attended by distinguished scholars, including Dr B. Ramarao, Former Director, National Ayurveda Research Institute for Panchakarma (NARIP), and Uttama Vaidya Pammi Satyanarayana Sastry, who participated as Guests of Honour.
The three-day programme featured intensive hands-on practical training and expert technical sessions conducted by distinguished scholars, including Shri Narasimha, Conservator, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) Library, Tirupati; Shri P.V.S. Kumar, Indic Manuscriptology Expert; and Uttama Vaidya Pammi Satyanarayana Sastry, Manuscriptology and Literary Expert.
Over 37 delegates, faculty members and postgraduate scholars participated in the practical sessions. The participants represented premier institutions, including S.V. Ayurvedic College, Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh; Rajarajeshwari Ayurveda Medical College, Humnabad, Bidar, Karnataka; and Basavaraj Patil Ayurveda College, Bidar, alongside research scholars and officers from CCRAS.
The workshop concluded with a valedictory session on the afternoon of October 28, 2026. Over the three days, participants gained extensive knowledge of palaeography, including manuscript deciphering, transliteration, editing, proofreading, text-critical analysis and script variants.

title: Scientists engage directly with farmers in Delhi’s rural areas under ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan'
subtitle: Scientists raise awareness among farmers about rabi crop management, balanced fertiliser use and sustainable agricultural practices
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 2:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare is organising the ‘Khet Bachao Abhiyan–Rabi 2026’ across the country from 22 October to 30 November 2026 through its two departments. The primary objective of the campaign is to ensure that farmers receive direct information about the latest agricultural technologies and government schemes through awareness programmes organised in villages. It also aims to raise awareness about the improved management of rabi crops and increased agricultural productivity through the adoption of modern technologies. The campaign is an important initiative towards developing agriculture for a developed India and ensuring the prosperity of farmers. Under the initiative, the concept of ‘Lab to Land’ is being put into practice, with agricultural scientists visiting farmers’ fields to share the latest scientific techniques, research-based knowledge and practical information that can help improve agricultural practices and productivity.
As part of this nationwide campaign, Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Ujwa, Delhi, is also conducting special awareness programmes in various villages across rural Delhi from 22 October to 30 November 2026. For this purpose, 25 locations have been selected across the South-West, North-West and North districts of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. These programmes are facilitating direct interaction between farmers and agricultural experts, enabling farmers to access scientific guidance and information relevant to their agricultural needs.
Each team constituted under the campaign comprises four to five subject-matter experts, scientists, officials from various departments and innovative farmers. Senior scientists from the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), Pusa, New Delhi, are also participating in these programmes, sharing the latest agricultural technologies and scientific knowledge with farmers. The teams are working to bridge the gap between agricultural research and its practical application in the field by providing farmers with relevant information and encouraging the adoption of improved farming practices.
Under the campaign, KVK Ujwa, Delhi, organised an awareness programme in Qazipur village on 27 October 2026. The main objective was to sensitise farmers to the importance of conserving soil health, carrying out agricultural operations at the appropriate time for the forthcoming rabi season, using fertilisers in a balanced manner and adopting natural farming practices. During the programme, KVK scientists provided information on maintaining soil fertility, undertaking essential agricultural operations at the right time and using fertilisers and other agricultural inputs scientifically and according to actual requirements. Particular emphasis was placed on adopting balanced fertiliser application based on soil health and ensuring the efficient management of agricultural resources. Farmers were encouraged to make informed decisions about the use of inputs to maintain soil productivity while supporting sustainable agricultural practices.
Keeping the upcoming rabi season in view, farmers were given detailed information about improved, high-yielding wheat varieties, appropriate crop management practices and the balanced application of fertilisers. They were also made aware of the importance of regularly monitoring mustard crops, identifying major pests and diseases at an early stage, and adopting appropriate management measures. These practices are intended to help farmers prevent potential crop damage, protect crop health and achieve better yields. The scientific guidance provided during the programme aimed to help farmers prepare for the season by adopting suitable crop-management measures and using agricultural inputs in accordance with crop requirements.
The programme also highlighted the importance of adopting sustainable agricultural practices, including natural farming, conserving natural resources and maintaining soil health. Farmers were encouraged to use the agricultural resources available to them judiciously and adopt environmentally friendly farming technologies. The emphasis was on promoting practices that support long-term soil fertility, improve resource-use efficiency and contribute to sustainable agricultural production. Through such direct engagement with farmers, the campaign seeks to strengthen awareness of scientific farming methods and encourage the practical adoption of sustainable agricultural techniques at the village level.

subtitle: Over 47 Lakh Sq. Ft. Cleaned Across 226 Sites; 4,602 MT Scrap Disposed of SECL Exceeds Targets for Physical and Electronic File Management; Cleanliness and Awareness Activities Undertaken Across Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh
date:

                28 OCT 2026 12:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, has surpassed several key targets under Special Campaign 6, achieving significant progress in cleanliness, scrap disposal, space optimisation and record management across its establishments in Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh.
SECL has undertaken cleanliness activities at 226 sites against a target of 225, covering more than 47 lakh square feet of area against the target of 40 lakh square feet.
Under the campaign, SECL has disposed of 4,602 metric tonnes of scrap against a target of 3,300 MT, generating revenue of approximately ₹26.17 crore. The achievements reflect the company's focus on efficient resource utilisation, systematic scrap disposal and improved workplace management.
Significant Progress in Record Management and Pendency Reduction
SECL has also recorded substantial progress in physical and electronic file management, surpassing its targets under Special Campaign 6.
Against a target of reviewing 500 physical files, the company has reviewed 2,100 files, while 872 physical files have been weeded out against a target of 200.
In electronic file management, SECL has reviewed 14,215 e-files against a target of 7,000 and closed 13,708 e-files against a target of 3,000, contributing towards reduction of pendency, improved record management and administrative efficiency.
E-Waste Management and Waste-to-Wealth Initiatives
With effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste being a key focus of Special Campaign 6, SECL has undertaken dedicated e-waste collection drives across its establishments.
At SECL Headquarters in Bilaspur, a dedicated e-waste collection bin was installed to facilitate the collection of discarded electronic items from employees. The bin itself was fabricated using discarded materials, demonstrating the concept of ‘Waste to Wealth’.
E-waste collection booths were also established in SECL's residential colonies in Bilaspur in, along with door-to-door collection activities to encourage participation by residents. Similar initiatives have been undertaken across SECL's operational areas.

As part of the campaign, SECL organised a range of cleanliness and awareness activities across its operational areas, including cleanliness rallies, Shramdaan activities, Nukkad Nataks, school-level competitions, awareness programmes and community participation initiatives.

The implementation phase of Special Campaign 6 was launched on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2026, with a Swachhata Happy Run, plantation under ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ and Swachhata Pledge at SECL Headquarters in Bilaspur.
Strengthening Good Governance and Workplace Efficiency
Special Campaign 6 is being implemented from 2 to 31 October 2026, with emphasis on e-waste management, cleanliness, space optimisation, scrap disposal, record management and reduction of pendency.
Through these initiatives, SECL continues to promote cleaner workplaces, responsible waste management, administrative efficiency and good governance, while encouraging greater participation of employees and communities in cleanliness-related activities.

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Interacts with Export Promotion Councils, Calls for Greater Export Competitiveness and Market Diversification

date:

                28 OCT 2026 10:19PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, interacted with representatives of Export Promotion Councils (EPCs) in New Delhi today to review the prevailing export scenario, discuss emerging opportunities and challenges in international trade, and deliberate on measures to further strengthen India’s export competitiveness.
During the interaction, Shri Goyal highlighted the evolving global trade environment, characterised by geopolitical uncertainties, changes in tariff structures, supply chain realignments and emerging regulatory requirements in major international markets. He noted that while these developments pose challenges for exporters, they also present opportunities for India to strengthen its position as a reliable and competitive global trading partner.
Shri Goyal emphasised the need for Indian industry to remain agile and responsive to the changing international business environment. He encouraged exporters to focus on improving product quality, innovation, cost competitiveness, reliability of supply and compliance with international standards to enhance India’s participation in global value chains.
Referring to his recent international engagements, including his visits to Germany and the Netherlands, Shri Goyal highlighted the growing interest in India as a manufacturing, sourcing and investment destination. He stressed the importance of translating these engagements into tangible business outcomes through sustained interaction between Indian industry and overseas businesses. He encouraged EPCs to engage proactively with their international counterparts, identify potential buyers and facilitate business partnerships in established and emerging markets.
The Minister also highlighted the importance of effectively leveraging the opportunities arising from India's expanding network of Free trade agreements and economic partnerships. He emphasised that preferential market access under Free Trade Agreements must translate into increased exports, greater market penetration and wider participation of Indian enterprises in international trade. EPCs were encouraged to undertake sector-specific assessments of export opportunities in partner countries and strengthen awareness among exporters regarding applicable trade preferences, standards and market requirements.
Shri Goyal also emphasised the need for a focused approach towards product and market diversification in response to changing global demand and emerging supply chain opportunities. He encouraged EPCs to identify products with untapped export potential, explore new destinations and develop market-specific strategies. He highlighted the importance of consolidating India’s competitive advantages in established sectors while building capabilities in emerging areas.
Reiterating the Government’s commitment to facilitating exports, the Minister highlighted ongoing efforts to improve ease of doing business, strengthen trade infrastructure and address challenges faced by exporting enterprises. He referred to the Export Promotion Mission as an important initiative for addressing constraints related to export finance, market access and international competitiveness, particularly for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs).
Highlighting the contribution of MSMEs to India’s export ecosystem, Shri Goyal called upon EPCs to expand their outreach to smaller enterprises, startups, new exporters and businesses in emerging export clusters and districts. He stressed the need for practical handholding support, improved access to market intelligence and greater integration of these enterprises into global markets.
The Minister further encouraged EPCs to adopt a more data-driven and outcome-oriented approach to export promotion. He emphasised the value of timely market intelligence, identification of sector-specific opportunities, monitoring of international trade trends and resolution of operational bottlenecks. He highlighted the need for greater collaboration among EPCs, industry associations, State Governments and field formations of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT).
During the interaction, representatives of the Export Promotion Councils also shared their perspectives on the international trading environment and sector-specific issues concerning export competitiveness, market access, logistics, regulatory requirements and trade facilitation. The discussions provided an opportunity to exchange views on addressing exporters’ concerns and strengthening coordination between the Government and industry.
Reaffirming the Government's commitment to maintaining regular engagement with industry stakeholders, the Minister underscored the importance of collective efforts to make Indian products and services globally competitive and strengthen India's reputation as a trusted trading partner.
The interaction reflected the shared commitment of the Government and Export Promotion Councils to work collaboratively towards expanding India's export footprint, harnessing emerging global opportunities and supporting sustainable, broad-based export growth.

title: GeM Samvad 2026 Highlights Reforms to Improve Public Procurement Access and Affordability for MSEs
subtitle:
GeM–LUB Partnership Facilitates 108 Virtual Conferences to Expand MSME Access to Government Procurement Opportunities

GeM Reduces Transaction Charges to 0.30%, Raises Exemption Threshold to ₹10 Lakh and Cuts OEM Assessment Fees by Up to 92%
date:
Posted On:
                28 OCT 2026 8:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Government e Marketplace (GeM), in collaboration with Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB), organised an event as part of GeM Samvad 2026 , highlighting key reforms aimed at making public procurement more accessible and affordable for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs).
Formalised through a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in 2024, the GeM–LUB partnership has facilitated 108 virtual conferences, apart from numerous physical events across India, to build awareness, support digital onboarding and help MSMEs navigate the platform and access government procurement opportunities.
In his address, CEO, GeM, Shri Mihir Kumar, stated that reforms undertaken by GeM have helped MSMEs by reducing participation costs, simplifying processes and improving access to finance, enabling them to participate more confidently in government procurement and contribute to the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047. He further stated that GeM endeavours to build a Trusted Seller ecosystem where business opportunities are completely democratised in digital format.
GeM has reduced transaction charges from 0.50% to 0.30% of the order value. Orders up to ₹10 lakh are exempt from transaction charges, compared with the earlier threshold of ₹5 lakh. For orders above ₹10 crore, charges are capped at ₹3 lakh, compared with the earlier maximum of ₹72.50 lakh. Nearly 97% of orders placed on GeM attract no transaction charges. The requirement for a Caution Money deposit as part of the onboarding process was also dispensed with in July 2025. Moreover, vendor assessment charges applicable to Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) have been reduced by 66% to 92% since January 2024.
As part of the event, President, LUB, Shri Madhusudan Dadu; National General Secretary, LUB, Shri Om Prakash Gupta; National Treasurer, LUB and GeM Nodal, Shri Janak Bhatia; and Additional CEO, GeM, Shri Ajit B. Chavan, participated in the deliberations and interacted with the MSMEs attending the event.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Ajit B. Chavan highlighted that, in line with the Union Budget 2026–27 announcement, GeM has integrated with all five Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) exchanges. He stated that this enablement, coupled with GeM SAHAY’s collateral-free lending against purchase orders on GeM, would go a long way in addressing the working capital and timely payment challenges faced by MSMEs.
President, LUB, Shri Madhusudan Dadu and National General Secretary, LUB, Shri Om Prakash Gupta outlined LUB’s plans to further deepen collaborative efforts with GeM and enhance outreach to MSMEs through LUB’s pan-India network of offices, regular weekly GeM–LUB virtual conferences and the setting up of dedicated facilitation counters at various offices, staffed by trained volunteers.

title: Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Meets H.S.H. Hereditary Prince Alois of Liechtenstein

date:

content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal paid a courtesy call on H.S.H. Hereditary Prince Alois of Liechtenstein on 28 October 2026 during his State Visit to India. The meeting focused on strengthening economic engagement and advancing investment opportunities under the India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA).
Shri Goyal highlighted India’s strong economic fundamentals, sustained reform agenda and expanding manufacturing capabilities, which offer significant opportunities for international investors. He underscored the Government’s continued efforts to improve the ease of doing business, simplify regulatory processes, strengthen digital governance and create a predictable, transparent and competitive business environment.
India’s investment performance reflects growing international confidence in its economic prospects. Cumulative Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) inflows stood at USD 843 billion during FY 2014-15 to FY 2025-26, with inflows reaching a record USD 94.53 billion in FY 2025-26, underscoring India’s growing attractiveness as an investment destination. India also has a thriving start-up ecosystem, with 2.50 lakh startups supporting over 25.42 lakh jobs across more than 770 districts and 56 industries. Of these startups, 52% are based in non-metropolitan cities.
Shri Goyal highlighted the opportunities offered by the India-EFTA TEPA, which entered into force on 1 October 2025. The Agreement provides for EFTA States to aim to increase FDI into India by USD 100 billion over 15 years and facilitate the generation of one million direct jobs. This framework offers an opportunity to translate stronger economic engagement into long-term investments, productive capacity, technology partnerships and employment generation in India.
Shri Goyal emphasised that India offers international businesses the advantages of a large and growing domestic market, a skilled workforce, a competitive manufacturing ecosystem and access to expanding global value chains. He invited companies from Liechtenstein to explore opportunities in India, including through manufacturing partnerships, technology collaboration, research and development, and deeper integration with Indian suppliers and micro, small and medium enterprises.
The discussions also explored opportunities to expand industrial cooperation in areas such as precision engineering, advanced manufacturing, industrial technologies and innovation. Greater collaboration in these areas can support technology adoption, strengthen industrial linkages and create mutually beneficial opportunities for businesses in both countries.
Earlier this month, on 7 October 2026, the India-EFTA Prosperity Summit was held in New Delhi to mark the first anniversary of the India-EFTA TEPA. H.E. Mr. Hubert Büchel, Minister of Home Affairs, Economy and Sport of Liechtenstein, along with representatives of Liechtenstein businesses, participated in the Summit.
The meeting reaffirmed the shared interest in leveraging the India-EFTA TEPA to strengthen investment flows and deepen commercial engagement. India’s focus remains on translating the opportunities created by the Agreement into tangible economic outcomes, including greater investment, enhanced manufacturing capabilities, technology collaboration and quality employment.

title: India and Mexico launch Negotiations for Preferential Trade Agreement, Sign Terms of Reference
subtitle: India and Mexico Discuss Expanding Trade and Investment Ties; PTA Negotiations Cover Key Trade Areas
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 10:38AM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mexico and India take an important step towards strengthening their economic and trade relations with the signing of the Terms of Reference for negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), which establish the framework, scope, modalities and roadmap for negotiations aimed at creating new economic opportunities for both countries.
The signing formally launches negotiations for a mutually beneficial and balanced PTA, with the potential to expand bilateral trade, create business opportunities, enhance investment flows and contribute to resilient and diversified supply chains.
The initiative follows the understanding reached between Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and President Dr. Claudia Sheinbaum during their meeting on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Canada in June 2025, when the two leaders agreed to further strengthen and deepen the India-Mexico partnership.
During the visit of Commerce Secretary, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, both delegations discussed bilateral relations and opportunities to expand trade and investment flows. The discussions were held with Mexico’s Undersecretary of Foreign Trade, Luis Rosendo Gutiérrez Romano, who participated on behalf of Secretary of Economy Marcelo Ebrard Casaubon.
The Terms of Reference cover key negotiating areas, including market access for goods, rules of origin, customs procedures and trade facilitation, dispute settlement, sanitary and phytosanitary measures, technical barriers to trade and trade remedies.
The proposed agreement seeks to leverage the complementarities between the two economies and expand opportunities for Mexican products and businesses in the Indian market. With its strong linkages to global value chains, Mexico is an important market for Indian exporters and investors. Sectors with significant potential for cooperation include automotive, chemicals, electronics, pharmaceuticals, agri-food, energy, critical minerals, medical devices and advanced manufacturing, among others.
The delegations also discussed various aspects of the bilateral economic agenda, identifying opportunities to deepen trade and investment relations, strengthen cooperation and foster closer ties between the productive sectors of both countries.
Both sides further discussed the possibility of organising a Mexican business mission to India during the first quarter of 2027. The proposed mission would facilitate business-to-business meetings, help identify commercial opportunities and strengthen commercial ties between the productive sectors of the two countries.

title: DoT Leads Thematic Session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ at ESTIC 2026
subtitle:
Session highlights AI-native 6G networks, quantum-safe communication, cybersecurity and indigenous telecom technologies

C-DOT and BSNL showcase telecom technologies, while Sanchar Saathi and Samridhh Gram are featured at outreach stalls
date:
Posted On:
                28 OCT 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, led the thematic session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ on 28 October 2026 at the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from 27 to 29 October 2026. Chaired by the Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, the session brought together experts from industry and academia to discuss emerging communication technologies and their role in building secure, intelligent and resilient digital infrastructure.
In his opening remarks, Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications said, “India has one of the largest, most affordable telecom networks with 1.2 billion mobile network connections  and 5G services in almost every district with one of the fastest 5G rollouts in the world. Department of Telecommunications has been supporting indigenous R&D efforts from the laboratory to the market through the Telecommunications Technology Development Fund, or TTDF, and we have so far supported over 130 projects worth to the tune of about ₹ 500 crore. In addition, through the Technology Development and Investment Promotion Scheme, with an outlay of again over ₹ 200 crore, recently renewed for the five-year period up to 2031, we are also helping startups and micro, small, and medium enterprises to join the global standardization, and test solutions in live networks.”
Delivering the keynote address, Mr. N. G. Subramaniam, Chairman, Tejas Networks Ltd., spoke on ‘Engineering Intelligent, Post-Quantum Networks: Autonomous and Trusted’. He highlighted how artificial intelligence, quantum-safe technologies and blockchain can complement one another, AI can enable network intelligence and automation, quantum-safe technologies can strengthen confidentiality and cryptographic resilience, and blockchain can support shared trust and accountability. He emphasised that trust must be engineered into next-generation networks.
The session also featured invited presentations on practical applications of intelligent and secure networks. Ms. Meenal Gupta of Easiofy Solutions presented ‘AI-Powered Medical Imaging over Quantum-Secure Intelligent Healthcare Networks’, illustrating how AI-enabled medical imaging can be supported by high-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity and quantum-safe security to facilitate faster, scalable and secure diagnostics, including beyond major urban centres. Mr. Himamshu Khasnis of Signalchip Innovations spoke on ‘Intelligent and Secure Radio Access Networks: From Chips to Systems’, highlighting indigenous radio-access-network chips and systems, AI-enabled network optimisation and adaptation, and advanced and post-quantum security. His presentation also outlined the role of domestically developed chipsets, radio units and base-station solutions in strengthening India’s telecom technology ecosystem.
A panel discussion brought together experts from academia and industry, including Prof. Rohit Budhiraja, IIT Kanpur; Prof. Bhaskar Kanseri, IIT Delhi; Ms. Sonali Garg, Senior Manager, HFCL; Dr. Ravi Parkash Gandhi, Chief Revenue Officer, Reliance Jio; and Mr. Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Director General, Bharat 6G Alliance. The discussion was moderated by Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, Centre for Development of Telematics (C-DOT). The panel exchanged perspectives on intelligent networks, quantum communication, cybersecurity and the development and adoption of indigenous telecommunications technologies.
The session also provided a platform to discuss India’s longer-term vision for intelligent and quantum-secure networks. The accompanying vision document identified priority areas including indigenous 6G technologies, AI-native networks and AI-driven cyber defence, a national quantum-secure backbone, zero-trust and cyber-resilience, and skills development. It also emphasised stronger links between research, testbeds, industry and commercial deployment.
DoT’s participation in ESTIC 2026 extended beyond the thematic session to technology and public-outreach showcases. At the thematic stall, C-DOT and Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) jointly showcased technologies and solutions relating to quantum communication and Mission Critical Services. At the Ministry/Departmental Outreach Stall, DoT showcased the Sanchar Saathi and Samridhh Gram initiatives, highlighting their public-facing applications and societal relevance.
The exhibition also provided dedicated spaces for deep-tech start-ups to showcase mature technologies across the Conclave’s 12 thematic areas.
DoT continued its active participation in ESTIC, building on its engagement in ESTIC 2025, where it led the thematic session on ‘Digital Communication’, by leading the session on ‘Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication’ at ESTIC 2026. Through these engagements, DoT has fostered collaboration among industry, academia and research institutions to advance indigenous telecom innovation, next-generation technologies and India’s future telecom ecosystem.
About ESTIC
The Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 is being held from 27 to 29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the theme ‘Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies’. Organised by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser, with CSIR–National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (NIIST) as the organising partner, the Conclave was inaugurated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 27 October 2026.
The Conclave brings together stakeholders from government, academia, research institutions, industry, deep-tech start-ups and the scientific community to deliberate on emerging technologies and their contribution to Viksit Bharat@2047. Its programme includes plenary talks, 12 thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, presentations by science and technology leaders and start-ups, exhibitions, poster presentations, and business-to-business and business-to-government meetings. The thematic areas include advanced manufacturing, energy technologies, synthetic biology, ocean and maritime technologies, intelligent networks and quantum communication, semiconductors, agri-tech, generative and autonomous artificial intelligence, robotics, advanced healthcare, immersive technologies and space science.
The Conclave also features distinguished international scientific personalities, including Nobel Laureates Prof. Joachim Frank, Sir Richard J. Roberts and Prof. Kostya Novoselov, alongside eminent Indian and international science and technology leaders. ESTIC serves as a national platform for showcasing technological advancements, identifying emerging scientific priorities and strengthening collaboration among research, industry and government.

title: India’s Cultural Consciousness and Knowledge Traditions Form the Foundation of Its Civilisational Continuity: Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat
subtitle: Book ‘Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’ launched in collaboration with IGNCA and ASI
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 8:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Highlighting the preservation of India’s cultural identity, the revival of monuments and the discourse on the nation’s historical memory, the book
Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi
was launched on today through a collaboration between the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA). The book has been published by IGNCA and Subhi Publications and edited by Tarun Vijay. The event was held at Dharohar Bhawan, ASI, Mandi House, New Delhi, with Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat as the Chief Guest. Dr. Jitendra Singh, Minister of State for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, attended as the Guest of Honour. Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe, former Rajya Sabha Member and former President of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), delivered the keynote address. The session was chaired by cultural thinker Dr. Anil Goyal.
The welcome address was delivered by Shri Y. S. Rawat, Director General, Archaeological Survey of India. The inaugural address was delivered by Prof. (Dr.) Ramesh C. Gaur, Dean, School of Arts, Media and Design, South Asian University. Shri Tarun Vijay, author and editor of the book, noted journalist and former Rajya Sabha Member, spoke about the book’s content and objectives. The vote of thanks was delivered by Prof. K. Anil Kumar, Head of the Kala Nidhi Division, IGNCA.
Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries, but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, spiritual practice, struggle and experience. India’s civilisation and cultural consciousness have flowed uninterrupted through the centuries. India has established connections with civilisations across the world through dialogue and cultural exchange. Its knowledge traditions, architectural heritage and cultural legacy have attracted countries across the world.
He said that during colonial rule, efforts were made to weaken Indians’ sense of pride in their civilisation, culture and traditions. This also influenced the way Indians viewed their own knowledge traditions and cultural ideals. The distinctive feature of Indian civilisation is its ability to draw inspiration from the past while moving towards the future. Ideals represented by Lord Rama and Lord Krishna, along with the traditions of sages, thinkers and seekers of knowledge, remain important foundations of India’s cultural consciousness.
Dr. Jitendra Singh appreciated the book and commended its editor, cultural thinker, author and senior journalist Shri Tarun Vijay, for bringing out a significant publication that highlights the importance of preserving and revitalising India’s cultural identity.
Dr. Vinay Sahasrabuddhe said that understanding India’s ancient culture and its timeless journey requires an awareness of, and pride in, its cultural heritage. He observed that, for a long time after Independence, there had been an unnecessary hesitation in speaking openly about Indian culture, making it difficult to break completely free from the colonial mindset. Books such as
Timeless India
provide an opportunity to understand India’s cultural continuity and the essence of Indianness.
Referring to Mark Tully’s book
No Full Stops in India
, he drew attention to a distinctive characteristic of the Indian mind. He said that the Indian mind does not seek to undermine the faith of ordinary people, but rather to understand their beliefs and lived experiences. The journey of Indian civilisation has been one of continuity, dialogue and change, and cannot be confined to a single conclusion or a limited perspective.
He emphasised that alongside publishing and preserving books, it is equally important to encourage the habit of reading. Indian culture should not remain confined to books but should become part of education and everyday life. He stressed the need to promote education in the mother tongue and to bring content related to Indian life and culture to students. He added that understanding India’s timeless cultural journey from an appropriate perspective and freeing the education system from colonial influences are important needs of the present time.
Dr. Anil Goyal while delivering his chair remarks  said that India is an ancient civilisation and a cultural consciousness shaped by a living tradition that has flowed for thousands of years. Despite numerous invasions and changes, India’s cultural spirit remains alive. Its temples, stupas, forts, sculptures and inscriptions are not merely historical monuments, but testimonies to the knowledge, art, science, faith and philosophy of its ancestors. He said that preserving heritage is a responsibility towards national identity, cultural continuity and future generations.
He emphasised the need to understand Indian history through facts and evidence and to bring forgotten achievements to light. Stressing the importance of understanding cultural heritage free from colonial influences, he said that a country should be assessed through parameters that reflect its social and cultural realities. Development and heritage, modernity and tradition, and science and culture are not contradictory but complementary. Books such as
Timeless India
play an important role in broadening understanding of India’s civilisational continuity and cultural heritage.
On the occasion, scholars, historians and intellectuals highlighted the importance of India’s civilisational continuity, cultural heritage and the preservation of its historical legacy through
Timeless India
.
A Book Focused on Monument Preservation and Cultural Memory
Timeless India
explores the role of monuments in preserving and revitalising India’s cultural identity, alongside the discourse surrounding the nation’s historical memory. The title points to India’s cultural continuity, which remains evident through different historical periods, architectural traditions and forms of cultural heritage.
The book gives particular importance to monument preservation and the idea of “decolonising the nation’s memory”. This perspective highlights the need to understand India’s cultural heritage through its own historical experiences, traditions and cultural outlook.
The launch presented the publication as an important initiative towards preserving Indian cultural heritage and broadening the discourse around it. The event also provided an opportunity to advance dialogue on culture, history, archaeology and cultural studies.

content:
Union Minister of State for Education, Shri Jayant Chaudhary today felicitated 10 National level winning teams and innovators of Viksit Bharat Buildathon (VBB) 2025 in New Delhi. The Guinness World Records certification for VBB 2025 as the “Largest Innovation Solution Competition,” was also presented at the function, marking a historic milestone for school education and grassroots innovation in India. As part of the Event, the Minister also launched the ‘Guidelines for Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs) under ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram’. He also distributed prizes to the student winners of the quiz competition based on e-waste.
Addressing the Event, Shri Jayant Chaudhary reiterated the importance of fostering confidence, creativity, innovation and independent thinking among children to mould them into future leaders. Highlighting the Buildathon Initiative, he noted that students were encouraged to identify problems and develop solutions independently, without predefined problems or solutions. He appreciated the participation of lakhs of students nationwide and acknowledged the role of teachers in mentoring and guiding them.
Expressing concern at the growing challenge of e-waste, Shri Chaudhary stressed on the need to involve schoolchildren in addressing it, thereby paving the way for its systematic management. He added that it was the shared responsibility of institutions, communities and citizens to address the issue.
Acknowledging the role of ULLAS in promoting adult literacy and restoring learners' dignity and confidence, he said that the new Guidelines would enable student teachers to play a vital role in empowering the nation.
Secretary, DARPG, Ms. Nivedita Shukla Verma; Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar; senior officials of the Ministry of Education; representatives and heads of autonomous bodies, education departments of States/UTs and partner institutions, attended the Event.
Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025
Organised by the Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog, and the All-India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), VBB 2025 was initiated to foster creative problem-solving, entrepreneurship, and scientific curiosity among school students. Centred around four foundational pillars—Atmanirbhar Bharat, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local, and Samriddh Bharat—the Initiative witnessed an unprecedented grassroots response, recording 2,87,967 project submissions across both Idea and Prototype tracks.
To evaluate the solutions, a rigorous, three-tier assessment framework was instituted at the district, state and national levels led by multidisciplinary expert panels. Following comprehensive evaluations, 10 national awardees, 100 state awardees and 1,000 district awardees were selected.
An award pool of over ₹1 crore was instituted across district, state and national levels. The 10 national winning teams were awarded a total cash prize of ₹17.50 lakhs . Under the Prototype Track, each of the five top winning teams was awarded ₹2,50,000, recognizing their functional working models. Each of the five winning teams under the Idea Track received ₹1,00,000 to encourage the incubation and scaling of their creative concepts. The winners who were felicitated today belonged to Assam, Delhi, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Keralam, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.
Special Campaign 6.0
Initiatives taken by both the Departments (DoSEL and the Department of Higher Education) under the Ministry under Special Campaign 6.0 highlighting the efforts to generate awareness about e-waste and e-waste collection endeavours, were presented at the Event. Secretary, DOSEL, Shri Anil Kumar also handed over the e-waste collected during the Campaign to the authorised recycler/refurbisher.
Under the Campaign, DoSEL had undertaken extensive drives to promote responsible e-waste management in schools across the country. Several activities were organised in schools today, including handing over of collected e-waste to authorised recyclers/refurbishers, e-waste-themed morning assemblies and e-waste based quizzes.
Guidelines for TEIs under ULLAS
The ‘Guidelines for Teacher Education Institutions (TEIs) under ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram’ released at the Event, envisages the participation of student teachers enrolled in NCTE-recognised teacher education programmes such as B.Ed., B.P.Ed., M.Ed., M.P.Ed. and other recognised programmes as Volunteer Teachers.
Under the Guidelines, each student teacher will be required to facilitate the literacy and certification of five to eight non-literate learners, with provision for academic credits linked to successful learner certification. Developed by DoSEL after extensive consultations with concerned stakeholders, the Guidelines also clearly define the roles and responsibilities of NCTE, NCERT, CNCL, SCERTs, DIETs, State Literacy Mission Authorities (SLMAs), District Authorities, TEIs and student teachers for effective implementation.

content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today emphasised the need to translate global biodiversity commitments into effective implementation, sustainable financing and lasting conservation outcomes at a side event of the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP-17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in Yerevan, Armenia. The event was organized by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Government of India, in partnership with
India’s
National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP). The event was also graced by Mr. Hambardzum Matevosyan, President of CBD COP17 and Minister of Environment of the Republic of Armenia, besides Dr. Taukondjo Shikongo, Head of Access and Benefit-sharing (ABS) unit, Secretariat of the CBD.
Delivering the keynote address at the side event titled -
From Policy to Practice: Advancing India's Biodiversity Commitments through Innovation, Finance, ABS and OECMS
- Shri Yadav highlighted the importance of building implementation capacity, sustaining finance and ensuring that biodiversity conservation and sustainable use contribute to human well-being and intergenerational equity. Referring to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, the Minister said that the responsibility of countries extends beyond adopting targets to building the capacity and mobilising the resources necessary to implement them.
Shri Yadav highlighted that biodiversity in India is inseparable from people's lives, knowledge and livelihoods. He emphasised that environmental protection and development must reinforce each other. The Minister also highlighted the principle of LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment), noting the importance of sustainable choices and responsible consumption in maintaining a harmonious relationship with nature.During the event, the dignitaries released four publications, that are as follows:
Guidelines for the Designation of India's Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (I-OECMs) 2026:
The guidelines would support the recognition of conservation outcomes beyond conventional protected areas, subject to appropriate criteria and governance. They recognise that effective conservation can take place across diverse landscapes and management systems.
5th National Report on Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety:
The report reflects the importance India attaches to transparent reporting and responsible biosafety governance.
The Convention on Biological Diversity Handbook:
Reference Guide and Indian Perspective:
The handbook aims to strengthen informed participation and continuity in implementation by providing accessible reference material on an increasingly complex international process.
India's ABS Success Story:
The book highlights India's position as a Globally acknowledged leader in Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS).
The Minister noted that these publications address interconnected priorities, including identifying conservation contributions, strengthening institutional understanding and reporting on implementation. He emphasised that ambitious biodiversity goals require sound guidance, reliable information and public accountability. The Minister called for measuring progress not merely by announcements or resources mobilised and areas identified, but by implementation, benefits delivered and sustained conservation outcomes.
Highlighting the importance of Access and Benefit Sharing, Shri Yadav said that the Nagoya Protocol provides a basis for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources. He stressed the need to translate this principle into workable, transparent and equitable procedures. India's experience, he noted, demonstrates the importance of complementing policy reforms with capable institutions, digital innovation and engagement with communities and responsible businesses.
Shri Yadav emphasised that no country can achieve the objectives of the Global Biodiversity Framework in isolation. He welcomed international cooperation that respects national priorities, promotes the exchange of practical knowledge and expands access to appropriate finance and technology. The Minister reaffirmed India's commitment to constructive dialogue, including South-South learning, and to approaches that enable countries to adapt successful ideas to their respective contexts. He expressed India's commitment to working with all Parties and partners in advancing the implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and to translate shared biodiversity ambitions into lasting results.
During the event, Mr. Hambardzum Matevosyan, Armenia’s Minister of Environment, and Dr. Taukondjo Shikongo, Head of the ABS Unit, SCBD, appreciated India's efforts in advancing biodiversity conservation and Access and Benefit Sharing. Their remarks underscored the importance of international cooperation and continued partnership in translating global biodiversity commitments into effective implementation.
