title: Union Government deputes High-Level Central Team to Investigate Death of Cheetah due to Firearm Pellet Injuries in Madhya Pradesh
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 7:52AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Government has taken serious note of the death of a 19-month-old male Cheetah (KNG22) of Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, due to firearm pellet injuries. Viewing the matter with utmost gravity, the Centre has deputed a high-level team for an on-ground investigation into the incident, given the critical importance of Project Cheetah and the need to ensure the highest standards of protection for the reintroduced population of the Big Cat.
The Central team comprises the Inspector General of Forests, National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), Additional Director, Wildlife Crime Control Bureau (WCCB), and Regional Deputy Director, WCCB. The team has been tasked with undertaking a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of the Cheetah, examining all available evidence and coordinating closely with the Madhya Pradesh Forest Department to ensure strict and swift action in the matter.
The Cheetah, an offspring of Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on 25th October 2026 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park. As reported by the Madhya Pradesh Forest Department, it was rescued from the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division the same day and provided intensive veterinary care and emergency surgery at the veterinary facility in Jabalpur. During the surgery, five firearm pellets were recovered from its body. Despite the medical intervention, the Cheetah succumbed to its injuries on 27th October 2026. Medical examinations corroborated multiple internal injuries associated with the recovered firearm pellets.
The State Government has already constituted a Special Task Force (STF), comprising Forest and Police officers, to investigate the incident. The Central team deputed by the MoEFCC would work in coordination with the State machinery. It would also examine the implementation of security protocols, as well as monitoring and protection measures being undertaken to avoid any such incident in future. The Central team would submit its findings and recommendations to the Ministry for further directions to the State Government and field authorities.

content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) continues its sustained crackdown on illicit trade and seized over 55,000 smuggled e-cigarettes at Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port, Kolkata, on 24th October 2026.
Acting on specific intelligence DRI officers intercepted two containers Nepal-bound transshipment consignment suspected to contain e-cigarettes. The goods had been mis-declared as “water glass” and “ceramic mugs” in another. A detailed examination of the first container led to the recovery of 40,000 pieces of e-cigarettes of brand IGET in various flavours, hidden among the declared cargo. Whereas, detailed examination of second container led to the recovery of around 15,000 pieces of e-cigarettes of various brands, including VTV, VOKO, Bang and Ejoy, hidden among the declared cargo.

Electronic cigarettes and all Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems (ENDS) are prohibited in India under the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes (Production, Manufacture, Import, Export, Transport, Sale, Distribution, Storage and Advertisement) Act, 2019, enacted in the interest of public health and to protect people from harm.

title: Union MoS Shri Prataprao Jadhav Launches Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign 4.0, Calls Upon Youth to Lead Nationwide Movement Against Tobacco and Addiction
subtitle:
Protecting Young People from Tobacco and Addiction is Essential for Building a Healthy, Strong and Viksit Bharat: Shri Prataprao Jadhav

Union Minister Administers ‘Say No to Tobacco’ Pledge, Urges Youth to Become Ambassadors of a Tobacco-Free India

Over 5.8 Lakh Educational Institutions and 73,000 Villages Declared Tobacco-Free Under Previous Three Editions of the Campaign

60-Day Nationwide Campaign to Intensify Tobacco Prevention, Strengthen Enforcement and Encourage Tobacco Cessation

Universities and Colleges at the Heart of TFYC 4.0; Special Focus on Tobacco-Free Campuses and Youth-Led Awareness

Six-Pronged Strategy and Whole-of-Government Approach to Drive Tobacco Control Efforts Across the Country
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 2:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Union Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, today launched the fourth edition of the Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign (TFYC 4.0) at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences (ABVIMS) and Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia (Dr. RML) Hospital, New Delhi, calling for a nationwide people's movement to protect young people from tobacco use and nicotine addiction.
The 60-day nationwide campaign, being undertaken by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, seeks to prevent tobacco initiation among young people, encourage tobacco cessation, strengthen enforcement of tobacco control laws and promote tobacco-free environments across the country. Building on the achievements of its previous three editions, which have seen over 5.8 lakh educational institutions and more than 73,000 villages declared tobacco-free, the fourth edition marks a significant expansion of the initiative, with universities and colleges emerging as a major focus of this year's campaign.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Prataprao Jadhav urged the country's youth to firmly reject tobacco and other addictive substances and embrace healthy, fulfilling and addiction-free lives. He emphasised that the health and well-being of young people are central to India's aspirations of becoming a developed nation.
Highlighting the pivotal role of young people in nation-building, the Minister said that India's youth are its greatest strength and that their energy, talent, creativity and determination will shape the country's future. He stressed that protecting the younger generation from tobacco and addiction is both a public health imperative and a national responsibility.
“Protecting our youth from tobacco and addiction is essential for building a healthy, strong and developed India,” Shri Jadhav emphasised, calling upon educational institutions, families, communities and government agencies to work together to create an environment in which young people can realise their full potential without the burden of addiction.
The Minister drew attention to the serious health consequences of tobacco consumption, noting that tobacco smoke contains more than 7,000 chemicals, including numerous toxic and cancer-causing substances, which can severely damage different organs of the body. He cautioned that tobacco use not only endangers the health of users but also exposes family members, children and others to the harmful effects of second-hand smoke.
Expressing particular concern about nicotine use during adolescence, Shri Jadhav observed that nicotine exposure at a young age can adversely affect brain development, attention, memory and learning abilities. He underlined the need to prevent tobacco initiation at an early age, when young people are particularly vulnerable to developing nicotine dependence.
Shri Jadhav stated that under the visionary leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the guidance of Union Health Minister Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda, the Government of India has been consistently strengthening its efforts to protect citizens, particularly children and adolescents, from the harmful effects of tobacco.
He noted that the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has been organising the annual 60-day Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign since 2023, focusing on tobacco prevention, cessation, stronger enforcement and community participation. The campaign, he said, has steadily evolved into a nationwide initiative bringing together students, teachers, educational institutions, enforcement agencies, healthcare professionals and communities.
Referring to the achievements of the previous three editions, the Minister highlighted that over 5.8 lakh educational institutions and more than 73,000 villages have been declared tobacco-free, reflecting the expanding reach of the initiative and the growing commitment of stakeholders across States and Union Territories.
He observed that the sustained efforts of the Government, supported by educational institutions and communities, have contributed to greater awareness about the dangers of tobacco and strengthened the country's tobacco control movement. Referring to national survey findings, including the Global Adult Tobacco Survey and Global Youth Tobacco Survey, he highlighted the importance of continued preventive efforts, particularly among adolescents aged 13–15 years.
The Minister emphasised that the campaign must transcend the boundaries of a government programme and evolve into a mass movement driven by the active participation and leadership of young people.
Recalling Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's message on de-addiction during his
Mann Ki Baat
address on 30 August 2026, Shri Jadhav said that the Prime Minister had called upon citizens to collectively work towards keeping India's youth away from addiction and ensuring that they lead healthy and addiction-free lives.
He urged young people to carry forward this message and become agents of change in their schools, colleges, families and communities.
Shri Jadhav called upon all stakeholders to take the message of ‘Say No to Tobacco’ to every corner of the country and ensure that tobacco prevention becomes a shared social commitment.
The Minister concluded his address by administering the ‘Say No to Tobacco’ pledge to all participants, reaffirming their collective commitment to staying away from tobacco, encouraging others to quit and contributing to a healthier, tobacco-free society.
Three Editions, Expanding Reach: Over 5.8 Lakh Educational Institutions and 73,000 Villages Declared Tobacco-Free
The launch of TFYC 4.0 builds on the achievements of three successive nationwide campaigns that have progressively expanded tobacco prevention activities, strengthened enforcement and mobilised educational institutions and communities across the country.
The first Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign, launched on 31 May 2023 to coincide with World No Tobacco Day, laid the foundation for a focused national effort to prevent tobacco use among young people. During the campaign, more than 1,42,184 educational institutions and 12,000 villages were declared tobacco-free. Enforcement activities under tobacco control laws resulted in fines exceeding ₹1 crore, highlighting the emphasis placed on regulatory compliance alongside awareness generation.
The second edition, launched in September 2024, significantly expanded the reach of the initiative through intensified awareness activities, enforcement drives and community participation. During this phase, 1,67,762 educational institutions and 27,534 villages achieved tobacco-free status, while strengthened enforcement measures resulted in fines exceeding ₹1.1 crore.
Building on this progress, TFYC 3.0, launched in October 2025, further consolidated the campaign's achievements. During its implementation, 2,57,807 educational institutions and 33,850 villages were declared tobacco-free.
The third edition also recorded substantial progress in enforcement and capacity building. More than 58,000 enforcement drives were undertaken, leading to 1,45,477 challans under Section 4 of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, which prohibits smoking in public places. In addition, more than 60,000 enforcement personnel and tobacco cessation counsellors were trained to strengthen tobacco control implementation and cessation support.
Taken together, the first three editions have seen over 5.8 lakh educational institutions and more than 73,000 villages declared tobacco-free, demonstrating the scale of the nationwide mobilisation and the growing ownership of tobacco control initiatives by institutions, local administrations and communities.
TFYC 4.0 Brings Universities and Colleges to the Forefront of Tobacco Prevention
A major distinguishing feature of Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign 4.0 is its dedicated focus on Higher Educational Institutions (HEIs), with universities and colleges being encouraged to play a more proactive role in preventing tobacco use and promoting healthy lifestyles.
Recognising that adolescence and early adulthood are critical stages for the initiation of tobacco use and the development of long-term health behaviours, the campaign seeks to engage young people at a stage when sustained awareness and positive peer influence can have a lasting impact.
Through its focus on higher educational institutions, TFYC 4.0 aims to strengthen tobacco-free campus environments, promote awareness about the harmful effects of tobacco and nicotine, encourage students to make informed health choices and mobilise educational institutions as active partners in tobacco prevention.
Universities and colleges will be encouraged to undertake awareness activities, strengthen compliance with tobacco-free educational institution guidelines, promote peer-to-peer engagement and actively involve students and faculty members in tobacco prevention efforts.
The initiative seeks to transform campuses into centres of tobacco prevention and youth-led action, enabling students to become advocates for healthier lifestyles not only within their institutions but also among their families and communities.
The special focus on higher education institutions adds a new dimension to the campaign by reinforcing the role of young people as participants, influencers and leaders in the national tobacco control effort.
Six Key Strategies to Drive TFYC 4.0 Across the Country
To translate the campaign's objectives into coordinated action, TFYC 4.0 will be implemented through six key strategies, combining awareness, institutional engagement, community mobilisation, enforcement and digital outreach.
The campaign will focus on:
Intensifying public awareness: Strengthening awareness and behaviour-change communication on the harmful effects of tobacco and nicotine addiction, particularly among children, adolescents and young adults, while motivating tobacco users to seek cessation support.
Strengthening Tobacco-Free Educational Institutions: Promoting compliance with the Tobacco-Free Educational Institutions (ToFEI) guidelines and encouraging schools, colleges and other educational institutions to establish and sustain tobacco-free environments.
Expanding Tobacco-Free Villages: Taking the Tobacco-Free Villages initiative to more communities by encouraging active involvement of local administrations, Panchayati Raj Institutions and community stakeholders.
Strengthening enforcement of tobacco control laws: Reinforcing implementation of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA), 2003, and the Prohibition of Electronic Cigarettes Act (PECA), 2019, through coordinated enforcement and compliance activities.
Leveraging social media and digital platforms: Expanding the reach of tobacco prevention messages through digital communication, social media campaigns and youth-oriented outreach to encourage greater public participation.
Engaging universities and colleges: Placing special emphasis on higher educational institutions to promote tobacco-free campuses, encourage student-led awareness and integrate tobacco prevention into campus health promotion activities.
These strategies are designed to strengthen tobacco control at multiple levels, with particular emphasis on preventing initiation, encouraging cessation and ensuring sustained compliance with existing laws and guidelines.
Whole-of-Government Approach to Strengthen Tobacco Control
TFYC 4.0 will adopt a comprehensive whole-of-government approach, recognising that protecting young people from tobacco requires coordinated action across health, education, youth development, local governance, law enforcement, communication and other sectors.
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare will strengthen collaboration with key Central Ministries, including the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Rural Development, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, and Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, among others.
Coordination with States and Union Territories, enforcement agencies, educational institutions and local administrations will remain central to implementation.
The campaign will also seek to deepen engagement with development partners, civil society organisations, healthcare professionals and community-based institutions to ensure wider outreach, effective implementation and sustained participation.
By bringing together diverse stakeholders, TFYC 4.0 aims to reinforce tobacco prevention as a shared responsibility and integrate tobacco control efforts into institutions and communities across the country.
Addiction-Free Youth Essential for Realising Vision of Viksit Bharat: Union Health Secretary
Addressing the gathering, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, emphasised that sustained commitment, coordinated institutional action and active community participation are essential for advancing India's tobacco control efforts.
She congratulated Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital on being a tobacco-free campus and appreciated the institution's initiatives in promoting tobacco control and creating a healthier environment for patients, students, healthcare professionals and visitors.
Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's vision of Viksit Bharat, the Health Secretary underlined that the country's progress depends significantly on the health, confidence, productivity and well-being of its young population.
She observed that a physically and mentally healthy, confident and addiction-free generation is essential for building a strong and developed India.
Urging young people to stay away from tobacco and other harmful addictive substances, she called upon them to embrace healthy lifestyles and contribute to a culture in which tobacco use is discouraged and positive health choices are encouraged.
She also highlighted the importance of sustained tobacco prevention activities in educational institutions and communities, stressing that collective action and behavioural change are crucial for achieving lasting results.
Patient Testimony and Awareness Films Highlight Human Cost of Tobacco Use
The launch programme witnessed the participation of over 300 people, including senior government officials, healthcare professionals, students, representatives of development partners, civil society organisations and members of the media.
Among the dignitaries present were Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; Dr. Loveneesh G. Krishna, Director General of Health Services; Dr. Akhilandeswari Prasad, Director, Dr. RML Hospital; and Dr. Yvan Hutin, WHO Representative to India, along with senior officials of the Ministry.
Students from ABVIMS also participated in the programme, reflecting the campaign's emphasis on the engagement of young people in tobacco prevention.
The event featured the screening of an educational video highlighting the harmful effects of tobacco and the importance of preventing tobacco-related diseases.
An important highlight of the programme was a patient testimonial under the Voice of Tobacco Victim (VoTV) initiative, in which a patient shared personal experiences of tobacco-related illness, bringing into focus the devastating consequences that tobacco consumption can have on individuals and their families.
A special campaign video was also screened, showcasing the achievements of the three previous editions of the Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign from 2023 to 2025. The video highlighted progress made by States and Union Territories in advancing tobacco-free educational institutions, tobacco-free villages, enforcement and community participation.
The awareness activities reinforced the campaign's central message that tobacco-related harm is preventable and that early prevention, informed choices and cessation support can help protect lives.
MoHFW Calls for Mass Participation to Make ‘Say No to Tobacco’ a Nationwide Movement
The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has called upon States and Union Territories, educational institutions, government departments, civil society organisations, development partners, healthcare professionals, youth organisations and citizens to actively participate in TFYC 4.0 and contribute to its nationwide implementation.
Stakeholders have been encouraged to undertake awareness activities, promote tobacco-free educational institutions and villages, strengthen enforcement, facilitate tobacco cessation and engage communities in sustained tobacco prevention efforts.
The Ministry has also urged institutions and citizens to amplify tobacco control messages through social media and digital platforms, share campaign activities and good practices, and encourage wider public participation.
By placing young people at the centre of the initiative and strengthening collaboration across government, educational institutions and communities, Tobacco-Free Youth Campaign 4.0 seeks to translate awareness into action and action into lasting behavioural change.
The fourth edition reinforces the Government of India's commitment to safeguarding the health of the younger generation and building a society where children and young adults can grow, learn and thrive free from tobacco and addiction.
With the message of ‘Say No to Tobacco’ at its core, TFYC 4.0 aims to inspire a nationwide movement led by young people and supported by every section of society, contributing to the vision of a healthy, addiction-free and Viksit Bharat.

Department of Water Resources, RD&GR, Ministry of Jal Shakti to support scientific groundwater recharge planning.
The mobile application enables users to identify potential artificial recharge zones within a radial distance of up to 3 km and explore suitable recharge structures based on local conditions.

title: Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi releases ₹1,000 Crore Margin Money Subsidy under PMEGP to support 11,333 new Micro Enterprises across India
subtitle: Landmark PMEGP support facilitates Bank Credit of ₹3,260 Crore, generates over 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities and promotes Inclusive Entrepreneurship in rural India
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 9:29PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, achieved another significant milestone in promoting self-employment and grassroots entrepreneurship with the release of ₹1,000 crore in Margin Money (MM) subsidy under the Prime Minister’s Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP).
The subsidy was released by Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME, during a special function organised by the Ministry at Kartavya Bhawan-3, New Delhi. The event was graced by Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State for MSME; Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME; other senior officials from the Ministry,
CEO,Khadi and Village Industries Commission
, CMD National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), and the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME).
PMEGP is one of the flagship credit-linked subsidy programmes of the Government of India aimed at creating sustainable self-employment opportunities through establishment of new micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector. The scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME is implemented nationally by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), with support from other designated implementing agencies such as KVIBs, District Industries Centres and Coir Board. Under the scheme, aspiring entrepreneurs are provided financial assistance in the form of MM subsidy on bank-sanctioned project loans for setting up new micro-enterprises. Awareness generation, handholding, capacity building, market linkages, monitoring and post-establishment support is also provided by KVIC field offices and Implementing Agencies at the grassroot level to promote long-term enterprise sustainability and growth. The programme plays a vital role in promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening local economies, and generating sustainable employment opportunities, particularly in rural and underserved regions of the country.
PMEGP's Transformational Impact since 2014-15
PMEGP has emerged as one of the country's most successful employment generation programmes. Since FY 2014-15, PMEGP has facilitated the establishment of more than 8.38 lakh micro enterprises through bank-sanctioned loans exceeding ₹ 70,000 crore and MM subsidy of over ₹ 25,193 crore, resulting in the generation of approximately 75 lakh sustainable employment opportunities across the country.
The achievements of PMEGP also reflect its strong commitment to inclusive and equitable development. Nearly 80% of the assisted units have been established in rural areas. Further, nearly 50% of the beneficiaries belong to SC, ST and OBC categories, while around 40% of the enterprises are owned by women entrepreneurs, demonstrating the scheme's pivotal role in fostering social inclusion, women-led development, and empowerment of disadvantaged sections of society.
₹1,000 Crore Subsidy to Benefit 11,333 Entrepreneurs to Date
The release of ₹ 1,000 crore MM subsidy will facilitate support to 11,333 beneficiaries under PMEGP. These beneficiaries have received bank-sanctioned project loans amounting to approximately ₹ 3,260 crore for setting up new micro-enterprises across various sectors.
The enterprises being established under this tranche are expected to generate more than 1.02 lakh sustainable employment opportunities, primarily in rural areas across the country. The assistance is strategically targeted to advance Women-led entrepreneurship and gender-inclusive growth; socially inclusive development, particularly among SC and ST communities; and balanced regional development, with a special focus on the North Eastern Region (NER) and Aspirational Districts.
Strong Performance During FY 2026-27
Prior to this release, during FY 2026-27, PMEGP had already supported 25,895 micro enterprises with MM subsidy amounting to ₹ 794.52 crore to October 2026. With the release of the present ₹ 1,000 crore subsidy tranche, the scheme is expected to further accelerate entrepreneurship development and employment generation across the country, strengthening the Government's vision of building a self-reliant, inclusive, and employment-oriented economy.
Speaking on the occasion, the Union Minister emphasized the critical role of micro enterprises in driving economic growth, fostering innovation, and generating livelihoods at the grassroots level. He reiterated the Government's commitment to ensuring that aspiring entrepreneurs, particularly those from rural areas, women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, and economically weaker sections, receive adequate institutional support to transform their entrepreneurial aspirations into successful enterprises.
The Ministry of MSME remains committed to expanding the reach of PMEGP and strengthening the entrepreneurship ecosystem to create sustainable livelihoods, promote local manufacturing and services, and contribute significantly to the vision of Viksit Bharat through inclusive and broad-based economic development.

title: Cabinet approves Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 3:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS), namely, the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY), a next-generation governance transformation initiative aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat. The scheme is approved for implementation from 2026-27 to 2030-31 (co-terminus with the Sixteenth Finance Commission period).
Financial implications:
The scheme outlay is Rs.7,395.55 crore, comprising a Central Share of Rs.4,869.48 crore and a State Share of Rs.2,526.07 crore.
Number of beneficiaries:
Around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. Each awareness-generation episode will reach at least 1 crore citizens.
Major impact including employment generation potential:
Support the preparation of 2.55 lakh holistic Gram Panchayat Development Plans annually on the eGramSwaraj Portal, bringing together village priorities, interventions of concerned Central and State departments, and available resources through participatory and evidence-based planning.
Reach at least 1 crore citizens in each coordinated awareness-generation exercise, using existing digital and outreach platforms, Gram Sabhas and other Panchayat forums to improve understanding of relevant Government schemes and national initiatives and encourage informed discussion of their local implications.
Strengthen governance capabilities of around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, annually, through capacity building and digital handholding to improve holistic planning, communication with citizens, resource management and progress towards locally relevant Sustainable Development Goals.
Support preparation of at least 2.55 lakh online audit plans annually and timely completion of the corresponding audits through AuditOnline. Alongside improved accounting, public disclosure, and Own Source Revenue mobilization, this will strengthen accountability for available funds and support more financially self-reliant Panchayats.
No permanent posts will be created under the scheme. However, the scheme may engage need-based contractual human resources at the State, District, and Block levels as part of the institutional mechanism to provide technical support and achieve its objectives.
States/districts covered:
The scheme will extend to all States/UTs, including institutions of rural local government (traditional local bodies) in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist.
Details:
Opportunity to take advantage of national transformational reforms at the grassroots level:
National reforms and Government initiatives undertaken over the past twelve years have created opportunities for strengthening village economies, improving public services and advancing rural development. Realizing these opportunities requires informed grassroots engagement and local planning that accounts for their implications. With the Sixteenth Finance Commission recommending around Rs.4.35 lakh crore in grants for Rural Local Bodies during 2026–27 to 2030–31, Panchayats need the capacity to bring together national priorities, Government schemes, available resources, and local aspirations. PM VGSY will support this approach through holistic planning, cross-departmental coordination, capacity building, and informed deliberations through Gram Sabhas. This will help translate national-level initiatives and enhanced financial resources into locally relevant development outcomes, furthering Viksit Bharat.
Gram Panchayats as hubs of local governance:
Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PM VGSY) will place the Gram Panchayat at the center of holistic local planning and coordination of development initiatives. Panchayats will be supported to bring together village priorities, relevant Government interventions, and available resources, enabling them to serve as the fulcrum of grassroots development. The scheme will connect the Viksit Bharat vision with rural communities' needs and aspirations.
Holistic planning at Gram Panchayat level:
The scheme will bring together the planning processes of all concerned Central Ministries /Departments and State Governments on a common digital platform to collaborate to prepare a holistic Gram Panchayat Development Plan (GPDP). This will help Panchayats and departments identify gaps, align interventions, and better use available resources, including Central Finance Commission grants. Existing departmental arrangements for delivering individual schemes will continue.
A user-friendly view of development in each Gram Panchayat:
Building on eGramSwaraj and existing e-Panchayat systems, the scheme will bring information on Government schemes, beneficiaries, benefits, community assets and available resources onto a common digital platform. This will help Panchayats identify gaps, address local needs and improve planning, coordination and monitoring.
Connecting National Priorities with Local Needs:
PM VGSY will use existing training, digital, and outreach platforms, including
PANCHAM
(an AI-enabled, multilingual, two-way communication platform in 17 Indian languages), to explain government schemes and national initiatives in simple, accessible language. Gram Sabhas and Panchayat platforms will encourage community discussions, helping connect national priorities with local needs and village development goals.
Capacity building to put the approach into practice:
Capacity building will support the effective use of digital platforms, interpretation of scheme and resource information, holistic planning and communication with citizens. It will help Panchayats translate available information and informed deliberations into locally relevant development plans and follow-up action.
Transparent and efficient utilization of available resources:
The scheme will strengthen Panchayats’ capacity to effectively utilize Finance Commission grants and other funds, mobilize Own Source Revenue (OSR), and ensure online accounting, auditing and public disclosure. This will promote transparent resource use, address local development gaps and foster accountable, self-reliant Panchayats.
Implementation strategy:
The scheme will be implemented through the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. States/UTs will submit Annual Action Plans specifying activities, priorities and requirements in accordance with the scheme’s objectives and guidelines. The designated Central Empowered Committee will appraise and approve these plans in accordance with applicable procedures and norms. The Central Government and States/UTs will undertake activities within their respective areas of responsibility, supported by coordination, technical assistance, monitoring and review. Existing institutional, capacity-building, digital, and communication systems will support implementation at the grassroots level.

title: Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, MoS for Power and New & Renewable Energy, leads Indian delegation to Singapore International Energy Week 2026
subtitle: Holds bilateral meetings with Singapore, Bhutan, IRENA and IEA on the sidelines
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 2:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Minister of State for Power and New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, led the Indian delegation to the Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW) 2026, held at the Marina Bay Sands Expo and Convention Centre, Singapore, from 26th to 28th October 2026.
SIEW 2026 coincided with the 25th year of Singapore's Energy Market Authority. The Summit was expanded into a two-day event this year and featured the Singapore-IEA Forum, the Singapore-IRENA Forum, and the IAEA at SIEW. Shri Naik participated and delivered a keynote on Day 1 and the Opening Remarks for the 2nd day of the event.
Addressing sessions on the first two days of the event, Shri Naik said India’s installed electricity capacity stood at 558.9 GW as of 30 September 2026, of which about 308 GW, or 55 per cent, came from non-fossil sources. He noted that India achieved 50 per cent non-fossil installed capacity in June 2025, five years ahead of its 2030 NDC target, and is now working towards 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030. Highlighting progress under the flagship schemes, he said that around 53 lakh rooftop solar systems had been installed under PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, benefiting about 63 lakh households. Under PM-KUSUM, nearly 12 lakh standalone solar pumps have been installed, and more than 17 lakh grid-connected agricultural pumps have been solarised, adding about 16.7 GW of decentralised renewable energy capacity and benefiting around 30 lakh farmers.
Shri Naik also held bilateral meetings with the following countries/organisations on the sidelines of SIEW 2026:
Singapore
: Shri Naik met Ms Gan Siow Huang, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Energy and Trade and Industry, Republic of Singapore. The two sides discussed energy cooperation under the India-Singapore Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including the proposed cross-border electricity interconnection between the two countries. Shri Naik invited long-term Singaporean investment in transmission, pumped storage, battery storage and renewable energy in India. Cooperation in green hydrogen and ammonia, energy efficiency, and partnerships between Indian power equipment manufacturers and Singapore's utilities was also discussed.
Bhutan
: Shri Naik met H.E. Lyonpo Sonam Tashi, Minister for Energy and Natural Resources, Royal Government of Bhutan, and congratulated him on assuming office. The two Ministers reviewed progress on the 1200 MW Punatsangchhu-I Hydroelectric Project, where dam works have progressed steadily since concreting resumed in April 2026, and noted the satisfactory operations of the 1020 MW Punatsangchhu-II project. They also discussed the other projects that are under discussion in partnership with Indian entities, along with the cross-border transmission planning up to 2040.
IRENA
: Shri Naik met Mr Francesco La Camera, Director-General, International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA). He appreciated IRENA's work as a platform for international cooperation on renewable energy and discussed deeper cooperation under the Strategic Partnership Agreement signed between MNRE and IRENA in January 2022. The discussions covered affordable finance for renewable energy in developing economies, long-term energy planning, green hydrogen and capacity building, including in the ASEAN region.
IEA
: Shri Naik met Dr Fatih Birol, Executive Director, International Energy Agency (IEA). Shri Naik welcomed the forthcoming launch of the IEA's India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026 at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and the India Critical Minerals Report at India Mining Week.
On the third day of his visit, the Minister visited Sembcorp's 326 MWh Battery Energy Storage System Plant at Jurong Island. Comprising of 800 large-scale lithium-ion phosphate batteries, the Sembcorp Energy Storage System on Jurong Island is the largest utility-scale battery energy storage system (ESS) in Singapore and Southeast Asia.
The tour concluded with a visit to Keppel's 800 TPD 22 MW Waste to Energy Plant in Tuas Region.
The visit provided an opportunity to share India's progress in the power and renewable energy sectors and to carry forward India's energy partnerships with Singapore and other partner countries and agencies.

title: Government Facilitating Startup-Industry Linkages to Take Indigenous Innovations to the Market, says Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh
subtitle:
Dr Jitendra Singh visits the exhibition at ESTIC 2026, featuring selected 50 deep-tech startups, 13 departmental stalls and 10 departmental technologies, reflecting the breadth of India’s scientific and technological capabilities

ESTIC-2026 Provides a Platform for Startups, Scientific Institutions and Industry to Explore Collaboration: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Indigenous Technologies Reflect India’s Growing Scientific and Technological Capabilities, says the Union Minister

Modi Govt Focused on Connecting Innovation with Practical Applications and Wider Adoption: Dr. Jitendra Singh

Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Stakeholders to Leverage Opportunities to Strengthen India’s Innovation Ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State for PMO, Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, has called for stronger linkages between StartUps and industry, emphasising the Government’s role in facilitating partnerships that can help indigenous innovations move from research and development to wider commercial adoption.
The Minister said that India’s expanding innovation ecosystem offers significant opportunities for startups to connect with industry and other potential technology adopters, develop practical applications and scale up their solutions. He urged stakeholders to come forward and make effective use of these opportunities to strengthen India’s innovation-led growth.
Dr. Jitendra Singh visited the exhibition of StartUps, scientific institutions and departmental technologies at the 'Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave' (ESTIC)-2026, being held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from October 27 to 29.
The conclave features selected 50 deep-tech startups, 13 departmental stalls and 10 departmental technologies, reflecting the breadth of India’s scientific and technological capabilities.
During his visit, the Minister reviewed a range of innovations demonstrating how scientific research is addressing challenges across sectors, from food and nutrition to advanced electronics. Among the exhibits was CSIR Designer Rice, a high-protein, low-glycaemic-index rice developed at CSIR–National Institute for Interdisciplinary Science and Technology (CSIR-NIIST).
The rice contains approximately 20 per cent protein and has a reported glycaemic index of 54, placing it in the low-GI category. Developed using rice fractions and structural modification, the innovation represents an effort to create food products with improved nutritional characteristics and potential relevance for people seeking better dietary management.
The exhibition also showcased JEET, the SCMC4212 microcontroller unit developed by Signalchip, reflecting India's growing capabilities in indigenous semiconductor and electronic-system design. Powered by a Yati 32-bit RISC-V CPU and an Avarta 32-bit digital signal processor, the microcontroller integrates memory, power-management and other functional capabilities in a compact design. Its potential applications include flight controllers, Internet of Things devices, smart devices, robotics and industrial automation. Such home-grown technologies can contribute to the development of domestic capabilities in strategic and emerging technology domains.
Other displays included bio-based packaging and reusable or application-specific products, illustrating the wider scope of innovation in materials and sustainability. Together, the exhibits demonstrate how India's scientific institutions, entrepreneurs and technology developers are working across diverse fields to develop solutions with practical applications, while creating opportunities for technology partnerships and commercial deployment.
Dr. Jitendra Singh has consistently advocated stronger coordination among research institutions, startups, industry and government to ensure that scientific discoveries translate into tangible economic and societal benefits. The exhibition at ESTIC-2026 provides an opportunity for startups to engage directly with prospective partners, identify applications for their technologies and explore pathways for scaling up their innovations.
The Minister urged industry leaders, investors, research institutions and other stakeholders to actively engage with startups and indigenous technology developers, build mutually beneficial partnerships and help take promising Indian innovations to wider markets. Stronger collaboration across the innovation ecosystem, he said, can help accelerate technology adoption, strengthen domestic technological capabilities and advance the national vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave 2026
subtitle:
Called on the scientific community, researchers and young innovators to deliver concrete, measurable and scalable technological outcomes

Dr. Jitendra Singh highlights India’s rise as a global co-creator in science and technology and calls for stronger biotechnology capabilities

Prof. Ajay K. Sood calls for closer alignment of research, industry and policy across ESTIC’s 12 priority domains

Nobel Laureates Joachim Frank and Richard Roberts address advances in structural biology and life sciences at ESTIC 2026

Parallel sessions deliberate on advanced manufacturing, generative and autonomous AI, and system and synthetic biology

ESTIC 2026 brings research, industry and policy leaders together to advance science-led innovation
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 10:01AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The inaugural day of the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 brought together more than 5,000 global delegates, including scientific leaders, policymakers and deep-tech startups, at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on October 27. The day’s programme combined addresses by national science and technology leaders, two Nobel Laureate plenary talks, three parallel technical sessions, a startup exhibition and poster track, an evening panel discussion along with the inaugural session. Across these proceedings, the focus was on connecting foundational research with industrial scale-up, public purpose and the development of technologies that can strengthen India’s capabilities and contribute to global welfare.
In his inaugural address, Prime Minister Sri Narendra Modi called on the scientific community, researchers and young innovators to deliver concrete, measurable and scalable technological outcomes within a three-year operational horizon. He emphasised that scientific breakthroughs should move beyond laboratory settings to address real-world problems, reinforce national self-reliance under the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat, and advance human welfare. The address also reaffirmed India’s commitment to setting global benchmarks in frontier areas, including artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, advanced materials and biotechnology.
Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, described a shift in India’s role in science and technology, from being a consumer of technologies to becoming a future-ready global co-creator of frontier scientific solutions. He highlighted the expansion of the country’s startup ecosystem from approximately 400 startups in 2014 to more than 2.3 lakh today. An estimated 50 to 60 per cent of these startups are based in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities, the Minister cited as evidence of the wider spread of technological entrepreneurship.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also identified India’s genetic and phenotypic diversity as an important resource for biotechnology and called for stronger domestic capabilities in gene synthesis, systems biology and nuclear medicine. He referred to recent legislative reforms, including the SHANTI Act, in the context of accelerating work in these fields. His remarks placed indigenous research capability and the development of applications from India’s scientific strengths among the priorities for the country’s biotechnology ecosystem.
Prof. Ajay K. Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, set out the need for closer alignment between basic scientific research, industrial scale-up and regulatory policy. He described ESTIC’s 12 core thematic priority domains and identified areas including quantum communication, generative and autonomous artificial intelligence, semiconductor fabrication, advanced manufacturing and the Deep Ocean Mission. His address situated the conclave as a forum for connecting research with the institutions, industrial capacities and policy frameworks needed to develop sovereign national capabilities.
Prof. Joachim Frank of Columbia University, the 2017 Nobel Laureate in Chemistry, delivered a plenary talk on cryo-electron microscopy (Cryo-EM) in target discovery and drug design. His presentation covered computational and mathematical frameworks used in high-resolution, single-particle Cryo-EM and the three-dimensional visualisation of macromolecular complexes. The session described how structural information about these complexes can support rational drug-design workflows and help researchers investigate biological targets.
Sir Richard J. Roberts, the 1993 Nobel Laureate in Physiology or Medicine, delivered a separate plenary on split genes and frontiers in life sciences. His talk covered the fundamental mechanisms of gene splicing, microbial genomics and restriction-modification enzymes. It also considered biotechnology initiatives relevant to sustainable agriculture, public health and diagnostics, linking advances in the life sciences with applications in food systems and healthcare.
Earlier, Dr. Jitendra Singh inaugurated the startup exhibition and poster track. The exhibition featured deep-tech research and development displays, startup prototype showcases and interactive poster presentations. It provided an opportunity for industry stakeholders, investors, academic researchers and policymakers to engage with research and emerging technologies across the conclave’s areas of focus.
The Advanced Manufacturing session, chaired by Dr. (Mrs.) N. Kalaiselvi, Director General of CSIR, featured a keynote address by Dr. G. Satheesh Reddy, former Chairman of the Defence Research and Development Organisation. The listed speakers included Shri Rajat Verma, Ms. Chaya Nanjappa, Dr. N. C. Murmu, Dr. C. Anandharamakrishnan and Dr. Nagahanumaiah. The session focused on implementing digital twins, collaborative robots, additive manufacturing and metrology, and on strengthening supply chains for micro, small and medium enterprises. These areas framed the discussion on how advanced manufacturing capabilities can connect research and engineering with industrial production and strengthen the domestic manufacturing base.
The Generative and Autonomous AI session was chaired by Shri Saurabh Vijay, Chief Executive Officer of IndiaAI, and featured a keynote address by Prof. Mitesh M. Khapra of IIT Madras. The session saw the participation of Prof. Chetan Arora, Dr. Alpan Raval, Prof. Balaraman Ravindran and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, among the key speakers. Discussion areas included the development of homegrown large language models, access to high-performance computing under IndiaAI, agentic artificial intelligence and frameworks for safe deployment. The session addressed the development of domestic AI capabilities and the conditions needed for responsible deployment of these technologies.
The System and Synthetic Biology session focused on engineered biological systems and the BioE3 national strategy. Its central framework was the “Understand, Design, Build, Test, Learn” cycle for biological design. The session identified precision biotherapeutics, metabolic pathway design, biofortified crops and waste-to-value biomanufacturing as areas of application. Together, these themes presented synthetic biology as a route from understanding biological systems to designing and testing them for applications in health, agriculture and manufacturing.
The evening panel discussion, “Science and Disruptive Technologies for Atmanirbhar Bharat,” was chaired by Prof. Ajay K. Sood. The listed panellists were Dr. Tessy Thomas, Gen. N. S. Raja Subramani, Prof. Bhanu P. Jena, Dr. Samir Saran and Prof. V. K. Singh. The discussion addressed defence technological sovereignty, commercialisation of intellectual property, deep-tech funding and mechanisms for technology transfer across sectors. These themes brought together questions of research translation, strategic capability and the movement of technologies between research institutions and industry.
ESTIC 2026 is organised around 12 thematic priority domains and brings together researchers, government, industry and startups. The Day 1 proceedings linked foundational science with practical work in advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence and engineered biological systems, while the plenary sessions addressed developments in structural biology and the life sciences. The Day -1 sessions identified the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation Fund and ANRF mechanisms as avenues for advancing deep-tech development through technology-readiness stages towards commercialised products. The conclave’s stated purpose is to strengthen the connections that enable science and technology to contribute to national development and wider human welfare.

title: Cabinet approves Rs 10,000 Crore Scheme to Make India a Global Container Manufacturing Hub
subtitle:
Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to raise domestic capacity ten-fold to 7.5 lakh TEUs and strengthen India's maritime supply chain

Sonowal thanks PM Modi for Make in India push: A strong step to reduce import dependence and secure our logistics chain
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, today approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS), a Rs 10,000 crore programme announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 to build a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India. The scheme will run from FY 2027-28 to FY 2039-40, with three years for setting up facilities and ten years of production support.
The scheme will support new factories as well as the expansion of existing units. It aims to lift India's annual container manufacturing capacity around ten-fold, to 7.5 lakh TEUs, from about 70,000 TEUs today.
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping & Waterways (MoPSW), Sarbananda Sonowal
welcomed this announcement by thanking Prime Minister Narendra Modi for emboldening Make In India push in container manufacturing in the country.
"I express my heartfelt gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his visionary leadership. His Make in India push is giving our container manufacturers the confidence to build at scale, and this scheme is a strong step to reduce import dependence," Sarbananda Sonowal said.
India's trade depends on containers, but almost all of them are made abroad. India's container traffic is projected to grow from about 24 million TEUs in 2024 to 175 million TEUs by 2047 under the Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision, which makes home-grown capacity critical.
What the scheme offers
Interest Subvention Assistance (Rs 859 crore):
3 per cent a year on eligible term loans for greenfield plants of at least 1,00,000 TEUs a year and brownfield expansions of at least 25,000 TEUs a year.
Operational Expenditure Assistance (Rs 8,891 crore):
support for every container made to global shipping standards and sold by an eligible manufacturer,
to
bridge the cost gap with imports. Domestic content must rise from 70 per cent to 90 per cent.
Testing and Certification (Rs 150 crore):
common facilities, such as dynamic longitudinal impact testing, to reduce dependence on overseas testing.
Scheme management (Rs 100 crore):
administration, monitoring and capacity building.
Land at major ports:
leasing support at 25 per cent of the notified rate.
An Inter-Ministerial Steering Committee chaired by the Secretary, Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, will approve guidelines and sanction assistance.
The scheme is expected to create about 3,000 direct and more than 50,000 indirect jobs, in steel, components and logistics. It will also support ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. The government estimates it will generate about Rs 75,000 crore of economic output by FY 2039-40, more than seven times the support provided. Demand is expected from replacement of the global fleet, the Bharat Container Shipping Line, and new mega ports such as Vadhavan and Galathea Bay.
"Containers are the backbone of our trade. By making them in India, we strengthen the maritime logistics supply chain on which our ports, our exporters and our shipping lines depend, and we take another step towards a self-reliant India and the goals of Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047," Sonowal added.

title: India’s Thoothukudi Mega Shipyard Picks Up Pace as Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal Meets HD Hyundai Chairman Chung Ki-sun in Seoul
subtitle:
Joint Working Group (JWG) to steer progress; JV structure to be worked out with DPR expected within Six months

Technology transfer and workforce skilling at heart of Thoothukudi plan, with Indian industry and academia to be brought in

Thoothukudi Shipyard envisaged as a Flagship Initiative under the India–Republic of Korea Special Strategic Partnership

Strategic partnerships, technology collaboration and localised manufacturing: Sarbananda Sonowal on HD KSOE’s India role
ministry: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Sarbananda Sonowal
, today met
Chung Ki-sun, Chairman of HD Hyundai
, in Seoul and discussed the next steps for India’s proposed greenfield shipyard at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. The meeting took place during Sonowal’s four-day visit to South Korea, which is focused on deepening India–Korea cooperation in shipbuilding and the wider maritime industry.
The meeting added momentum to the project, and the day’s engagements produced a clear path forward. HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering (HD KSOE), HD Hyundai’s shipbuilding arm, reiterated its intent to participate as a primary strategic investor, and the project partners expressed their shared intent to take the yard forward. A joint working group (JWG) will now oversee project development, the two sides will work towards agreeing a joint venture structure, and the Detailed Project Report (DPR) is expected to be finalised within six months.
Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal told HD Hyundai Chairman Chung Ki-sun that his main goal in Seoul is to turn into reality, as quickly as possible, the shared vision the Chairman had set out to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, that India is a core pillar of HD Hyundai’s global future, as India–Korea maritime ties gain new energy since President Lee Jae Myung’s visit to New Delhi earlier this year.
Speaking at the meeting,
Sarbananda Sonowal
said, “We have a clear mandate to scale up our work together. The MoU we signed on 20 April 2026 is the bedrock of what we want to build together in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu. A greenfield shipyard with $4 Billion investment is a massive milestone, and we are completely committed to backing it. Your team has done an incredible job during the site assessment and has been continuously collaborating with the teams from both  Central as well as the State governments.”
National Shipbuilding & Heavy Industries Park, Tamil Nadu Limited (NSHIP-TN) and HD Korea Shipbuilding & Offshore Engineering Co., Ltd. (HD KSOE) expressed their shared intent to take forward the proposed greenfield shipyard at Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu.
The discussions built on the India–Republic of Korea Comprehensive Framework for Partnership in Shipbuilding, Shipping and Maritime Logistics adopted in April 2026 and the Memorandum of Understanding signed on 20 April 2026 between HD-KSOE and NSHIP-TN on the sidelines of the state visit by the President of the Republic of Korea, H.E. Lee Jae Myung. During the meeting HD-KSOE expressed its appreciation of the enabling conditions created by the Government of India towards implementation of the project.
The proposed shipyard, being developed under the Government of India's Shipbuilding Development Scheme, is envisaged to have an annual shipbuilding capacity of approx.
2.5 million Gross Tonnage (GT)
, subject to validation through Detailed Project Report (DPR). Once operational, it is expected to be India's largest commercial shipyard, significantly strengthening domestic shipbuilding capacity and India's competitiveness in the global maritime industry.
During the meeting HD KSOE reiterated its strong intent in participating as a primary strategic investor, bringing its global expertise in shipyard design, construction, advanced manufacturing and operations. Discussions will now focus on finalising the proposed investment structure, equity participation and implementation arrangements, subject to due diligence and requisite approvals. Similarly, NSHIP-TN reassured its support for setting up of the greenfield shipyard, including all coordination with the government authorities both at Central as well as the State level.
Speaking about the domestic demand in India,
Sarbananda Sonowal
said, “The domestic market in India is booming right now. Our public agencies are looking to acquire more than 400 vessels in the coming years. I am sure that apart from the export orders the mega greenfield shipyard in Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu would be instrumental in construction of many of these identified vessels. We look forward to HD KSOE deepening its footprint in India through strategic partnerships, technology collaboration and localised manufacturing, thereby contributing to India’s emergence as a global shipbuilding hub.”
To accelerate implementation, a working group comprising officials from both sides would oversee project development and coordinate key activities. The two organisations will endeavour to agree on a suitable joint venture structure and are expected to finalise the DPR within six months, covering vessel product mix, production capacity, infrastructure requirements, project costs and implementation schedule.
NSHIP-TN will facilitate the availability of suitable waterfront land, development of enabling infrastructure and utilities, and coordination with relevant authorities for timely statutory approvals, in accordance with applicable laws and procedures. In parallel, preparatory activities, including site assessments, infrastructure planning and preliminary dredging/reclamation studies, will be progressed to support project readiness.
Beyond infrastructure development, the collaboration aims to establish a
globally competitive shipbuilding ecosystem in India
, with emphasis on technology transfer and workforce skilling. Opportunities for technical training, knowledge exchange and collaboration with Indian industry and academic institutions will be explored to strengthen indigenous shipbuilding capabilities and generate skilled employment.
In his closing remarks,
Sarbananda Sonowal
said, “This partnership will be a truly vital & defining cornerstone of the broader India-Korea relationship. By bringing together South Korea’s world-class technological genius with India’s economic energy and market scale, we are creating a partnership that will genuinely reshape the global maritime landscape.Let’s join hands to bring this incredible shipyard to life on the ground. I am eager to hear your thoughts on how we can accelerate this journey together.”
The proposed Thoothukudi shipyard is envisaged as a
flagship initiative under the India–Republic of Korea Special Strategic Partnership
, combining Korea's advanced shipbuilding expertise with India's industrial capabilities and long-term maritime ambitions.

title: MSDE Calls Upon CPSEs to Accelerate Apprenticeship Engagement with Focus on Outcomes and Inclusion
subtitle: National Review of Central Public Sector Enterprises held at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) today convened the
National Review of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs)
at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi, with a focus on strengthening apprenticeship engagement across public sector enterprises and positioning apprenticeship as a mainstream pathway from learning to livelihoods.
The review underscored the need to reposition apprenticeship not as a fallback option, but as a
credible and aspirational pathway
that combines theoretical learning with practical workplace experience, enabling young people to acquire industry-relevant skills and become job-ready.
Emphasising the need to shift attention from scale alone to tangible outcomes, Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, said: “Apprenticeship must become a mainstream and aspirational pathway from learning to livelihoods. As the ecosystem expands, our focus must go beyond the number of apprentices engaged to what apprenticeship enables young people to become. CPSEs can play a catalytic role by expanding quality opportunities, improving participation of women and under-represented groups, and creating stronger pathways to productive employment. Our collective success should ultimately be measured through completion, certification, employability, absorption and retention.”
The apprenticeship ecosystem has achieved significant scale under the
National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS-2)
.
From FY 2022-23 to 22 September 2026,
44.75 lakh apprentices were engaged
,
supported by
47,452 active establishments
.
Optional Trades accounted for
76.27% of apprenticeship engagement
,
reflecting the increasing importance of flexible, employer-responsive apprenticeship pathways.
During the review, CPSEs were called upon to address the gap between apprenticeship potential and actual engagement through
realistic enterprise-wise intake plans
aligned with the applicable
2.5%–15% apprenticeship requirement
.
Enterprises were encouraged to validate their workforce and portal data, establish time-bound recruitment trajectories and nominate senior-level nodal officers to monitor implementation and resolve bottlenecks.
The National Review reinforced the collective responsibility of CPSEs, States and other stakeholders to strengthen apprenticeship as an integral component of India’s skilling and employment ecosystem and provide young people with meaningful pathways to gain workplace experience, industry-relevant skills and opportunities for sustainable livelihoods.

title: Union Secretary Shri Sudhansh Pant Reviews Implementation of Welfare Schemes in Assam
subtitle:
Shri Pant Appreciates Joint Efforts Of DoSJE And Assam Government Team In Implementing The Ministry’s Welfare Initiatives

Emphasises Sustained Inter-Departmental Coordination,  Outreach And Convergence For Effective Delivery Of Social Welfare Programmes To Eligible Beneficiaries And Timely Resolution Of Implementation Bottlenecks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, today reviewed the implementation of various welfare schemes of the Ministry in Assam, covering Drug Demand Reduction, Scheduled Caste Development, Senior Citizen Welfare, Sanitation Workers’ Safety And The Rehabilitation Of Vulnerable Groups.
The review meeting held at State Capital Guwahati, assessed the progress of key initiatives and highlighted the need for coordinated efforts to ensure that welfare interventions translate into tangible benefits for eligible beneficiaries.
The meeting was attended by Shri Ajay Tiwari, Additional Chief Secretary, Home and Political Department, Government of Assam; Shri Pallav Gopal Jha, Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and senior officers of the State Government.
During the review, Shri Pant emphasised the importance of a coordinated, whole-of-government approach to the effective implementation of social welfare programmes. He stressed that the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment should play an effective nodal role in bringing together the concerned departments and implementing agencies.
Shri Pant highlighted the importance of convergence under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) and the National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE). He appreciated the progress made by Assam and underscored the need for sustained efforts to address implementation gaps.
Strengthening Drug Demand Reduction and Rehabilitation
The Secretary was apprised that under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, awareness and outreach activities have covered all districts of Assam, reaching 27.71 lakh people through 6,575 activities across 10,614 educational institutions. The State has registered 13,712 Nasha Mukti Mitra volunteers and recorded 2,24,783 e-pledges, reflecting the participation of educational institutions, volunteers and communities in efforts to prevent substance abuse.
The State Officials informed the meeting that Assam has 16 Integrated Rehabilitation Centres for Addicts and six State Government-funded de-addiction and rehabilitation centres, in addition to other treatment and outreach facilities. These facilities support the broader efforts towards awareness, treatment, rehabilitation and social reintegration of persons affected by substance use.
Promoting Integrated Development and Livelihood Opportunities
The State Officials further informed that under PM-AJAY, 721 Scheduled Caste villages have been taken up for integrated development. The livelihood component has approved 5,269 beneficiaries, including women associated with Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and individual Scheduled Caste women, with an overall financial involvement of ₹26.34 crore. The scheme also envisages the construction of 28 mini stadiums in Scheduled Caste-dominated areas, supporting community infrastructure and opportunities for sports and physical activities.
The review emphasised the importance of effective implementation and convergence to ensure that development interventions create sustainable livelihood opportunities and improve access to essential facilities for Scheduled Caste communities.
Advancing Safety and Dignity of Sanitation Workers
The review also examined the implementation of NAMASTE, which seeks to promote the safety, dignity and well-being of sanitation workers through improved occupational practices and mechanisation. In Assam, 483 sewer and septic tank workers and 6,365 waste pickers have been profiled across 96 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).
The programme focuses on occupational safety, personal protective equipment, health coverage and mechanised sanitation practices. These interventions aim to improve working conditions, reduce occupational risks and strengthen the adoption of safer sanitation practices.
Strengthening Senior Citizen Welfare and Rehabilitation of Vulnerable Groups
The meeting further reviewed Senior Citizen Welfare under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), measures for the protection of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, and the rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging under the SMILE scheme.
It was informed that under the Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana, 10,715 senior citizens in Assam have been assisted, with 48,756 assistive devices distributed during the financial year 2026–27 up to 27 October 2026. The initiative facilitates access to assistive devices for senior citizens facing age-related disabilities and mobility challenges, supporting their independence and quality of life.
Strengthening Inter-departmental Coordination and Effective Implementation
Shri Pant appreciated the efforts of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment and the State Government team in implementing the Ministry’s welfare initiatives. He emphasised the need for sustained inter-departmental coordination, effective outreach to eligible beneficiaries and timely resolution of implementation bottlenecks.
The Secretary also highlighted the importance of systematically documenting and publicising success stories to showcase the impact of welfare schemes and create greater awareness among eligible beneficiaries. The review underscored the need for continued collaboration between the Central and State Governments to strengthen implementation mechanisms and ensure that the intended benefits of social welfare programmes reach people across Assam.
Through these coordinated efforts, the Ministry and the State Government reaffirmed their commitment to promoting social justice, inclusion and improved quality of life for Scheduled Castes, senior citizens, sanitation workers and other vulnerable sections of society.

title: From The Streets To Self-Reliance
subtitle:
A Journey Of Dignity And Renewed Hope

Rehabilitation And Livelihood Support Under The SMILE Scheme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 6:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
At 46,
Meera Thakur (name changed)
could transform her life from one marked by homelessness, illness and uncertainty to one defined by confidence, dignity and self-reliance. This could become possible by the strong support and encouragement through great initiative.
Her journey reflects the role of comprehensive rehabilitation and livelihood support under the
SMILE (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise)
Scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
A Class XI pass who had previously worked in flower garland making and catering assistance, Meera faced serious personal and financial difficulties following a breakdown in her family life. With limited support, she moved between places in search of shelter and employment.
After losing her savings and essential documents, she fell seriously ill, lost her livelihood and eventually became homeless. With no dependable source of income, she sought alms at temples and other public places to meet her basic needs and medical expenses. Suffering from acute anaemia and extreme weakness, she required medical attention, sustained care and a safe environment in which to rebuild her life.
On 16 March 2024, Meera was rescued from the premises of the District Court Shani Mandir in Indore Madhya Pradesh by the Param Pujya Rakshak Aadinath Welfare and Educational Society (PRAWES) team and brought into the rehabilitation system. She was admitted to Aurobindo Hospital, where she received medical treatment and nutritional support for severe anaemia. She also underwent successful cataract surgeries in both eyes, helping improve her vision and overall well-being.
Under the SMILE Scheme, she received comprehensive institutional care, including safe accommodation, medical treatment, psychological counselling and sustained rehabilitation support. This secure and supportive environment helped her regain physical strength, emotional stability and trust in others.
As her health improved, Meera began participating in yoga, meditation and music therapy sessions. She also took part in a cultural programme during Ram Navami, portraying Shabri in a theatrical performance that reflected her growing confidence and willingness to engage with others. She went on to acquire skills in making carpets and door mats from old sarees, tailoring, pearl garland making, incense-stick production and crafting eco-friendly products such as cow-dung idols, diyas and havan kunds. In July 2025, she participated in a workshop organised by the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), further strengthening her rehabilitation and skill-development journey.
Over time, Meera emerged as a responsible and respected member of the rehabilitation centre. She took on ward-management responsibilities and actively supported the well-being of fellow women residents. Today, she has moved beyond dependence on begging and is using her skills to earn a livelihood. She has taken responsibility for kitchen operations at the rehabilitation centre, independently preparing breakfast each day for approximately 50–60 beneficiaries. Her contribution reflects her culinary abilities, discipline and commitment to collective well-being.
Alongside these responsibilities, Meera participates in fairs, public markets and exhibitions to sell her handmade products, earning approximately Rs 8,000 per month. From an uncertain income of around Rs 200 per day through begging, she has progressed towards a more structured and dignified means of livelihood through handicrafts and other skills. She has regained confidence, developed leadership abilities and found new ways to contribute to the lives of others. She aspires to achieve greater financial independence, secure a stable livelihood and eventually live in an independent home with other rehabilitated women. She also hopes to use her experiences to support people facing similar hardships.
Meera’s journey demonstrates how rescue, healthcare, psychological support, vocational training and livelihood opportunities can work together to facilitate meaningful rehabilitation. Through sustained assistance under the SMILE Scheme, she has moved from vulnerability towards independence and from uncertainty towards renewed hope. Her story underscores the importance of a comprehensive rehabilitation approach that goes beyond immediate relief to help individuals rebuild their lives with dignity, confidence and opportunities for sustainable livelihood.
