title: From Financial Barriers To Global Innovation:  A Journey Of Ambition And Opportunity
subtitle: National Overseas Scholarship Enables SC Student to Pursue Higher Education at Brown University, USA
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Growing up in a middle-class Scheduled Caste family, Aarav Patel
(name changed)
aspired to build a career at the intersection of technology, business and innovation.
He envisioned establishing successful technology-driven enterprises and making a meaningful contribution to society through his work. However, limited financial resources, inadequate mentorship and a lack of professional networks in advanced science and engineering careers presented significant challenges.
The high cost of pursuing quality higher education at leading international universities posed a major financial barrier. In addition, limited access to experienced mentors and professional networks made it difficult to navigate advanced academic opportunities and understand potential career pathways in science and engineering. Despite these constraints, he remained committed to acquiring the knowledge, skills and global exposure necessary to pursue his ambitions.
The National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme provided crucial financial assistance, enabling him to pursue a Master of Science (MSc) degree at Brown University in the United States. During the financial year 2023–24, assistance amounting to US$ 89,816 was provided, with support approved on 26 June 2023. The assistance covered tuition fees, maintenance allowance, visa fees, medical insurance and travel expenses.
By addressing the substantial financial requirements associated with overseas education, the scheme helped the beneficiary access an advanced academic environment and acquire specialised knowledge, skills and credentials relevant to his professional aspirations. His international educational experience strengthened his understanding of technology, innovation and business development.
Today, the beneficiary is a business owner and director, working towards his ambition of building successful technology-driven enterprises. The qualification and exposure gained through his studies have provided him with a stronger foundation to pursue entrepreneurial opportunities. His family continues to belong to the middle-income segment, while the educational opportunity has expanded his professional horizons and equipped him with capabilities to pursue future growth.
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme reflects the Government of India's commitment to expanding access to higher education for eligible students from Scheduled Castes and other specified categories, in accordance with the scheme's guidelines. By supporting tuition and other essential expenses associated with overseas study, the scheme helps eligible students access international academic institutions, strengthen their professional capabilities and pursue their aspirations.
The beneficiary's journey demonstrates how targeted educational assistance can help bridge financial barriers, widen access to global learning opportunities and nurture the aspirations of future professionals and entrepreneurs. From overcoming financial constraints to pursuing global education and entrepreneurship, his story highlights the transformative potential of educational opportunity in building a foundation for innovation, ambition and social progress.

subtitle: Rehabilitation Support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts
date:

content:
Recovery from substance dependence help individuals rebuild their health, relationships and economic stability.
The journey of NEEL
(name changed),
a 25-year-old graduate from Karimnagar, Telangana, highlights the role of comprehensive rehabilitation and continued support in helping individuals work towards a healthier and more stable life.
NEEL began consuming alcohol and cannabis due to peer influence and family stress. Over time, substance use affected his work performance, health and family relationships. He experienced financial instability, social isolation, emotional disconnection and declining confidence. His family was also affected financially and emotionally, but continued to support him through treatment and rehabilitation.
On 22 May 2026, NEEL received support through the Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA) at Prakriti Environment Society in Karimnagar, Telangana. The assistance included medical treatment, detoxification, individual counselling, behavioural therapy, emotional and psychological support, and family counselling.
Vocational guidance, follow-up care and relapse prevention services further supported his recovery and helped him work towards rebuilding his personal and professional life.
Family motivation and comprehensive rehabilitation support helped NEEL develop healthier habits, strengthen family relationships and regain confidence. The combination of counselling, treatment and continued care supported his efforts to maintain sobriety and move towards a more stable and independent future.
Today, NEEL is maintaining sobriety, working regularly and earning approximately Rs 15,000 per month. His regular income has enabled him to contribute to his family’s well-being, while improved relationships and renewed confidence have helped him move forward with greater stability.
NEEL’s journey demonstrates the importance of accessible treatment, professional counselling, family participation and sustained follow-up care in supporting recovery from substance dependence.
The rehabilitation services provided through the IRCA at Prakriti Environment Society highlight how comprehensive support can help individuals rebuild their lives, restore family relationships and work towards social and economic reintegration.

As part of the observance of Vigilance Awareness Week 2026, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, organized an expert lecture on

, at the Ministry’s Headquarters in National Capital, here today.
The lecture was delivered by Director, Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), Smt Tamanna Sinha, who highlighted the importance of preventive vigilance in promoting transparency, accountability and integrity in government functioning.
Smt Sinha emphasized the role of vigilance administration in identifying and addressing potential risks of corruption, strengthening institutional mechanisms and promoting ethical practices in public service.
She highlighted there is a need to lay more emphasis on preventive measures to ensure that government processes are conducted with fairness, transparency and adherence to established rules and procedures.
Smt Sinha put up a detailed PowerPoint presentation covering various aspects of vigilance awareness and preventive vigilance. The presentation sensitized officers and officials on identifying potential vulnerabilities in administrative processes, adopting best practices and maintaining the highest standards of integrity while discharging their official responsibilities.
A Senior Official in the Ministry informed that a large number of officers and officials of the Ministry and the Department, participated in the session. He said special impetus was laid on the participation of personnel dealing with administrative, financial, procurement, establishment, legal and vigilance matters, given their role in ensuring compliance, transparency and accountability in government operations.
The Official said the interactive session provided an opportunity for the participants to deepen their understanding of preventive vigilance and its practical application in day-to-day official work.
The programme concluded with a renewed commitment by the participating officers and officials to uphold probity, accountability and ethical conduct in public service.
The observance of Vigilance Awareness Week reinforces the importance of collective responsibility in preventing corruption and fostering a culture of integrity, transparency and good governance across government institutions.

title: Workshop on Base Revision of State level Index of Industrial Production during 28–30 October 2026 at Thiruvananthapuram, Keralam
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 8:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The three-day Regional Training Workshop on Base Year Revision of the State Level Index of Industrial Production (IIP) commenced at Hotel Dimora International, Thiruvananthapuram, on 28 October 2026. The workshop was organized by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Government of India, in collaboration with Department of Economics & Statistics (DES), Government of Keralam. The workshop will continue until 30 October 2026.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, formally inaugurating the workshop.
The programme began with lamp lighting by the dignitaries. Inaugural session of the three days workshop was graced by the distinguished dignitaries, including the Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam and by Shri V. K.
Sreejan, Additional Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam. The Workshop was attended by approximately 60 participants from 16 States/UTs.
Ms. Shailamma K, Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam, welcomed the dignitaries and participants, acknowledged the support of MoSPI and organising the regional training programme, and highlighted the importance of strengthening the technical capacity of State statistical offices for the effective implementation of the IIP base-year revision exercise.
Shri Deepak Dhanawat, Director, MoSPI, outlined the objectives and background of the workshop. He has highlighted on the importance of State IIP in tracking the industrial performance if State. He stressed that States should compile the same methodology as the All India IIP.
Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, Special Secretary, Planning & Economic Affairs Department, Government of Keralam, presided over the inaugural session. In his presidential address, Shri Gokul G. R., IAS, highlighted the growing public importance of reliable official statistics in a context where economic information is widely discussed through social media and where individual participation in financial and retail investment has increased. He observed that timely, credible and methodologically sound statistics are essential for informed public discussion and evidence-based policy decisions. He stressed that the item basket used for compiling the IIP should reflect the current structure of industry and changes in production patterns. He also emphasised the need to strengthen the quality of primary data collection, minimise measurement errors and ensure that the information furnished by reporting units accurately represents industrial activity.
Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), MoSPI, formally inaugurated the workshop. In his inaugural address, Dr. Dalip Singh emphasised the need to align the revised State-level IIP series with the updated national methodology to improve consistency and comparability across States and Union Territories. He referred to 2022–23 as the proposed new base year and underlined the importance of updating the item basket so that the index captures changes in the industrial economy. He also drew attention to the need to improve the availability and quality of data for industrial products and minerals, including major and minor minerals, and to strengthen the systems used for collecting and validating data. The adoption of NIC 2025, appropriate treatment of sectors such as Gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management in line with relevant recommendations, and suitable value-based approaches for heterogeneous products were among the methodological considerations highlighted. He encouraged States to strengthen their capacity for regular monthly compilation of the IIP and to ensure that the revised series is robust, timely and comparable.
The revision of the base year from 2011–12 to 2022–23 is intended to ensure that the IIP better reflects the present industrial structure, changes in the range of products manufactured and evolving production patterns. The index is an important indicator for monitoring short-term movements in industrial production and supporting economic analysis and policy formulation.
The workshop is designed to provide practical and methodological guidance to officers from States
and Union Territories on the key stages of the revision exercise, including selection of the item basket and factories, item grouping, preparation of the weighting diagram, data sources and treatment of items classified as Not Elsewhere Classified (NEC). The programme also covers the review of NIC 2025, feedback on the revised National Product Classification (NPC), data-sharing mechanisms, and methodologies for substitution and imputation.
Dignitaries on the dais during the inaugural session
The first day's technical sessions included a presentation on the new features of the IIP base-year revision by Ms. Ankita Singh, Deputy Director General, MoSPI, followed by presentations on the progress of the revision exercise in States and Union Territories. Sessions also addressed sectors and data sources and the treatment of NEC items. Representatives from 16 States/Union Territories, numbering 60 in total, are participating in the workshop. The sessions scheduled for the following two days will focus on the technical and validation aspects of the revision, with opportunities for States to raise queries and share feedback.
The inaugural session concluded with a vote of thanks proposed by Shri V. K. Sreejan, Additional Director, Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Keralam. He expressed gratitude to MoSPI for organising the workshop and providing technical support and acknowledged the cooperation of the Government of Keralam and the participating officers from the States and Union Territories. He also conveyed his appreciation to the dignitaries, resource persons and officials involved in organising the programme.

subtitle: India's Index of industrial production records growth of 6.7% in September 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 4:00PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In September 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 6.7 % year-on-year growth, supported by 7.6 % growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 11.2 % in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.
The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28th of every month (or next working day if 28th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.
2.  Key Highlights:
The IIP growth rate for the month of September 2026 is 6.7 percent which was 8.0 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of August 2026.
The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of August 2026 are (-) 6.2 percent, 7.6 percent, 11.2 percent and 5.8 percent respectively.
The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 124.3 against 116.5 in September 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of September 2026 stand at 90.4, 128.0, 128.6 and 146.4 respectively.
Within the Manufacturing sector, 17 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in September 2026 over September 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of September 2026 are – “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (19.0 %), “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (33.9 %), and “Manufacture of rubber and plastics products” (19.9 %).
In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth.
In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment”, item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives” and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth.
In the industry group “Manufacture of rubber and plastics products”, item groups “Acrylic Sheets (Including PVC, Polystyrene/Polycarbonate and Other Plastic Sheets)”, “Tyres for Light Motor Vehicles (LMV)”, and “V-Belts and Rubber Conveyors” have shown significant contribution in growth.
As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 111.6 for Primary Goods, 153.4 for Capital Goods, 131.7 for Intermediate Goods and 133.0 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month of September 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 133.1 and 111.8 respectively.
The corresponding growth rates of IIP as per Use-Based Classification in September 2026 over September 2025 are 4.0 percent in Primary Goods, 10.4 percent in Capital Goods, 12.2 percent in Intermediate Goods, 7.2 percent in Infrastructure/ Construction Goods, 6.0 percent in Consumer durables and 1.4 percent in Consumer non-durables (Statement III).  Based on Use-Based Classification, top three positive contributors to the growth of IIP for the month of September 2026 are Intermediate Goods, Primary Goods and Capital Goods.
Along with the Quick Estimate of IIP for the month of September 2026, the indices for August 2026 have undergone final revision in the light of the updated data received from the source agencies.
The Quick Estimates for September 2026 and the final revision for August 2026 have been compiled at weighted response rates of 86.5 percent and 92.0 percent respectively.
Details of Quick Estimates of the Index of Industrial Production for the month of September 2026 at Sector, Sub-Sector, 2-digit level of National Industrial Classification (NIC-2025), by Use-Based Classification and are given at Statements I, II (A, B, C, D) and III respectively. Also, for users to appreciate the changes in the industrial sector, Statement IV provides month-wise indices for the last 13 months, by industry groups (as per 2-digit level of NIC-2025), sectors and Sub-Sectors.
Release of the IIP for October 2026 will be on Monday, 30th November 2026.

title: Ministry of Textiles to Open PLI Scheme Portal for accepting new applications from 1st November 2026
subtitle: Minimum Turnover criterion for Part 2 of the Scheme reduced to ₹100 Crore
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 6:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ministry of Textiles is set to reopen the application portal for the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles for accepting new applications under
Round 4
of the Scheme
from 1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026
to promote the manufacturing of Man-Made Fibre (MMF) Apparel, MMF Fabrics and Technical Textiles, enhance domestic manufacturing capabilities, attract investment, generate employment and strengthen India's position in global textile value chains.
To facilitate wider participation under the Scheme, the following key modifications have also been made in the Scheme:
1. Reduction in Minimum Turnover Criterion:
The minimum turnover requirement has been reduced from ₹200 crore to ₹100 crore under Part 2 category of the scheme, enabling greater participation by MSMEs and mid-sized manufacturing units.
2. Extension of Scheme Tenure:
The scheme tenure has been extended up to Financial Year 2033–34 exclusively for applicants approved under Round 4. The extended tenure is intended to provide these applicants with a longer investment and operational horizon for establishing and scaling up their manufacturing capacities.
3. Migration of Existing Participant Companies of the Scheme to Round 4
: All existing participant companies of Round 1, 2 & 3, in any part of the Scheme, that have not claimed or received any incentive so far, are also eligible to migrate under Round 4, subject to withdrawal of their existing applications under Round 1, 2 and 3, as applicable.
The online application portal
https://pli.texmin.gov.in
will remain open from
1st November 2026 till 31st December 2026
. Eligible companies are encouraged to submit their applications within the stipulated period in accordance with the applicable scheme guidelines.

The Indian Culinary Institute (ICI), an institute under the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi, today at Kartavya Bhawan, New Delhi. The recognition of ICI

s BBA and MBA programmes by JNU, commencing from the next academic year, is expected to enhance academic and professional opportunities for students. The collaboration will facilitate access to higher education and improve employment and placement prospects for graduates, both in India and abroad, while contributing to the growing demand for skilled professionals in India

title: Tawang to Host 14th International Tourism Mart from 29–31 October 2026
subtitle:
Ministry of Tourism to organise the three-day Mart in Arunachal Pradesh to showcase the tourism potential of the North Eastern Region

Over 200 participants, including domestic and international buyers and sellers, expected to participate in the Mart

Regional Meeting of Tourism Ministers of North Eastern States to be chaired by Union Minister for Tourism and Culture
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 9:50AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, is organising the 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM) for the North Eastern Region from 29–31 October 2026 at Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh. The three-day event will be held at Hotel Vivanta, Tawang, bringing together domestic and international tourism stakeholders to showcase the region's diverse tourism potential and strengthen business partnerships.
The inaugural programme on 29 October 2026 will be attended by the Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister for Tourism and Culture, Shri Suresh Gopi, Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas  and Shri Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh. The inaugural programme will include the inauguration of the North East Bazaar and cultural performances highlighting the region's rich traditions.
The International Tourism Mart is an annual flagship event of the Ministry of Tourism aimed at promoting the North Eastern Region as a tourism destination in domestic and international markets. The Mart serves as a platform for tourism businesses, entrepreneurs, tour operators, government agencies, media and other stakeholders to explore opportunities for collaboration, strengthen tourism linkages and promote the region's rich natural, cultural and adventure tourism offerings.
Over 200 participants, including domestic and international buyers and sellers, are expected to participate in the 14th International Tourism Mart. The event is expected to witness participation from 43 international buyers representing 22 countries, including Australia, Bhutan, France, Germany, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Poland, Russia, Singapore, South Korea, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, the United Kingdom and the United States, among others. The Mart will also bring together domestic buyers, tourism service providers and sellers from the eight North Eastern States, facilitating business interactions and opportunities for collaboration.
The Mart will showcase destination and tourism product presentations by all eight North Eastern States—Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim and Tripura. These presentations will highlight the distinctive tourism attractions, experiences and offerings of each State, along with combined tourism circuits and products of the North Eastern Region.
The event will also feature Business-to-Business (B2B) sessions on 30 October 2026, facilitating structured interactions between domestic and international buyers and tourism service providers from the North East. These engagements are aimed at promoting business collaborations, developing tourism products and strengthening market access for tourism entrepreneurs and service providers from the region.
Technical sessions during the Mart will focus on key aspects of tourism development in the North Eastern Region. These will include discussions on building the live events and concert economy in the North East, led by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, and facilitating tourist access to Protected and Restricted Areas in the region, led by the Ministry of Home Affairs. A presentation by Royal Enfield on
'Beyond Destinations: Creating Immersive Journeys in North East India'
will explore opportunities for experience-based tourism in the region.
The event will feature the North East Bazaar, highlighting the region's traditional arts, handicrafts, textiles and cultural heritage. Cultural performances and regional cuisines will further offer delegates an opportunity to experience the distinctive traditions and culinary diversity of the eight North Eastern States.
As part of the Mart, technical visits have been planned to prominent tourist attractions in and around Tawang, including Tawang Monastery, Jaswant Garh War Memorial, Jang Waterfall, Tawang War Memorial, Urgelling Gompa—the birthplace of the 6th Dalai Lama—Buddha Park, Pankang Teng Tso (PTSO) Lake and Shernup Village. These visits will provide participants with first-hand exposure to the region's spiritual heritage, natural landscapes, local traditions and rural tourism experiences. Familiarisation tours for international delegates are also scheduled to commence from Guwahati on 1 November 2026.
Along the sidelines of the Mart, a Regional Meeting of Tourism Ministers of the North Eastern States will be held on 30 October 2026, chaired by the Union Minister for Tourism and Culture. The meeting will provide a platform for discussions on strengthening tourism development in the North Eastern Region and enhancing cooperation among the States.
The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart marks its return to Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, after 13 years, with it having last hosted the 2nd edition in 2013. The previous edition of the Mart was held in Gangtok, Sikkim, in November 2025.

title: MY Bharat Organises ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad: Know Your Vote’ Across 14 States/UTs to Promote Electoral Awareness
subtitle: Youth Take Loktantrik Pledge to Uphold Democratic Values and Strengthen Civic Participation
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 10:20PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat), under the Department of Youth Affairs, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, organised editions of
Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvaad: Know Your Vote
across educational institutions in 10 States and 4 Union Territories today as part of its nationwide campaign to promote electoral awareness and encourage informed and responsible participation of young people in democracy. The events brought together students, public representatives, Youth Icons, accomplished sportspersons and institutional leaders for discussions on voting rights, civic responsibilities and democratic values.
The nationwide campaign, being conducted across 500 universities, colleges and institutions from 26.10.2026 to 05.11.2026, aims to provide young people, including first-time voters, a platform to interact directly with elected representatives and exchange ideas on democratic participation in the journey towards Viksit Bharat@2047. As of 28 October  a total of 27 Yuva Samvaads have been conducted across the country, with 5,856 young people participating in the programmes.
In the Northern Region, programmes were today held at institutions in Delhi, Gurugram, Panchkula, Rajouri and Jhajjar. At Shri Ram College of Commerce, the event was attended by Shri Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, along with sportspersons Shri Arjun Singh Nagra and Shri Ajeet Yadav. The programme in Panchkula and the event in Sunderbani also saw participation by students and young citizens in large numbers.
In the Central Region, programmes in Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh focused on electoral awareness, youth leadership and responsible citizenship. In Sheopur, Member of Parliament Shri Shivmangal Singh Tomar interacted with students on voting rights and the electoral process. In Raigarh, the dialogue was held alongside the Neighbourhood Youth Parliament in the presence of Lok Sabha MP Shri Radheyshyam Rathia and MY Bharat Joint Director Shri Raman Patel.
In the Eastern Region, MY Bharat Darjeeling organised a Youth Samvaad in Phansidewa. The programme featured a presentation on the Viksit Bharat Young Leaders Dialogue (VBYLD), interactive discussions on ‘Know Your Vote’, a voter-awareness pledge and a Signature Wall reaffirming participants’ commitment to democratic values. Other programmes were held in Bihar and West Bengal.
In the North-Eastern Region, the programme at Rajiv Gandhi University in Arunachal Pradesh featured Youth Icon Porbindar Kaur and Commonwealth and South Asian karate gold medallist Johny Mangkhiya.
In the Southern and Western Regions, programmes brought together students, Youth Icons, sportspersons and invited dignitaries for discussions on electoral processes, civic responsibilities and democratic participation.
The programmes concluded with the administration of the Loktantrik Pledge, through which participants resolved to uphold democratic values and participate actively in the democratic life of the nation. The
Know Your Vote
online quiz competition, organised by MY Bharat in collaboration with MyGov, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, was also promoted to raise awareness about the electoral process. MY Bharat registrations were facilitated at the venues, and suggestions from participants were collected through QR-based suggestion boxes.

content:
The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme with a total outlay of Rs.1,856.67 crore for the period 2026 to 2033-34. The scheme aims to promote investment, manufacturing, innovation and exports, and strengthen India's position in the global sports goods sector.
Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, the Scheme seeks to strengthen India's sports goods manufacturing base through targeted support for investment, technology adoption, research and innovation, skill development, quality certification and market development. The scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India's position in global supply chains.
Aligned with the vision of Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat, the Scheme is expected to attract investment, create employment opportunities, strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities and enhance the global competitiveness of Indian sports goods.
Building Integrated Sports Goods Manufacturing Ecosystems:
The Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems through the co-location of manufacturers, suppliers, testing facilities, design and prototyping centres, and ancillary enterprises. These Zones will be developed through convergence with existing industrial infrastructure under the BHAVYA Scheme and NICDC Industrial Parks, enabling efficient manufacturing, stronger industry linkages and enhanced competitiveness across the sports goods value chain.
These zones will support the creation of integrated manufacturing facilities, strengthen industry linkages and improve operational efficiencies. These interventions are expected to facilitate investment, enhance production capacities and support the growth of a robust sports goods manufacturing base in the country.
Attracting Investments and Expanding Domestic Manufacturing:
A key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth.
Together, these interventions, backed by a combined outlay of Rs.1,130 crore, are expected to strengthen domestic manufacturing, reduce import dependence, enhance domestic value addition, catalyse significant private investment, generate employment opportunities across the value chain, and improve India's competitiveness in global markets.
Strengthening MSMEs and Existing Manufacturing Clusters:
Recognising the important role of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the sports goods sector, the Scheme places emphasis on strengthening existing manufacturing clusters and supporting the growth of smaller enterprises.
Assistance will be provided for the upgradation of existing sports goods manufacturing clusters, including the development of common facilities and shared infrastructure.
Promoting Quality and International Certification:
The Scheme recognises the importance of internationally accepted quality and performance standards in enhancing the competitiveness of Indian sports goods.
Support will be provided to manufacturers for obtaining and renewing certifications from International Sports Federations, with an outlay of Rs.105 crore.
These measures will help improve product quality, facilitate access to international markets and strengthen confidence in Indian-made sports goods.
Investing in Research, Technology and Innovation
The Scheme places special emphasis on strengthening research, design and innovation in the sports goods sector.
Support will be provided for the establishment of Centres of Excellence in premier educational and research institutions to promote research in sports equipment, material sciences, protective gear and advanced manufacturing technologies.
Research and development activities will also be encouraged through convergence with the Anusandhan National Research Foundation.
Dedicated support for start-ups, in alignment with the Startup India initiative, will foster innovation and facilitate the development, testing, validation and commercialisation of new technologies, processes and products within the sports goods manufacturing ecosystem.
Developing a Skilled Workforce for the Future:
Recognising the employment-intensive nature of the sports goods sector, the Scheme will support skill development initiatives aligned with industry requirements.
The skill development initiatives will be implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and relevant industry stakeholders to ensure alignment with evolving industry requirements.
These efforts will help meet the growing demand for skilled manpower and support the long-term development of the sports goods manufacturing sector.
Taking Indian Sports Goods to Global Markets:
The Scheme seeks to expand India's presence in international sports goods markets through dedicated branding, outreach and market development initiatives. Leveraging the Export Promotion Mission, these efforts will enhance the visibility of Indian sports goods, strengthen market access and support their greater penetration in international markets.
Supporting India's Global Sporting Ambitions:
By promoting the manufacture of high-quality and internationally certified sports goods, the Scheme will support the evolving requirements of India's sports sector and athlete development programmes. Enhanced innovation, quality infrastructure and manufacturing capacity under the Scheme will complement initiatives such as Khelo India and Fit India.
The Scheme is expected to position India as a globally competitive hub for the design, development and manufacture of sports goods. By strengthening manufacturing capabilities, promoting innovation and expanding global market access, it will create new opportunities for growth, employment and exports, while supporting India's aspiration to emerge as a leading sporting nation and advancing the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047.

title: Sports and Education Ministries sign historic MoU with UNESCO to take clean sport values to every classroom
subtitle: Sporting Excellence and Sporting Integrity should go hand in hand, says Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Union Education Minister Shri Pralhad Joshi on Wednesday reaffirmed the need to integrate sports and education, which is also highlighted in the Khelo Bharat Niti 2025, as the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’.
The MoU was exchanged at the National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA) India’s Clean Sport Conclave here, with the initiative aimed at embedding values such as respect, integrity and fairness in children through education, sports and everyday classroom activities. The toolkit’s video modules will be made available in 13 Indian languages, with the objective of reaching students across the country and building a stronger, fairer sporting ecosystem.
Besides Dr. Mandaviya and Shri Joshi, present in the conclave were Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis, Secretary, Dept of School Education, Ministry of Education, Shri TK Anil Kumar, Secretary, Sports, Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Shri Hari Ranjan Rao and DG NADA, Shri Anant Kumar. International delegates who attended the statutory meetings of the UNESCO anti-doping conventions on Tuesday, were also in attendance. India international javelin thrower Sachin Yadav also took part in the conclave.
Dr. Mandaviya expressed his sincere appreciation to the Education Ministry, stating the collaboration reflected the Government of India’s commitment to bringing sports and education together, in line with Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision. “Sporting excellence and sporting integrity must go hand in hand. Talent, discipline and hard work are essential for sporting success, but integrity, fairness and credibility are equally important,” the Hon’ble Sports Minister said, highlighting the need to strengthen clean sport awareness alongside India’s growing sporting ambitions.
He also mentioned about India’s 4th place finishes at the Asian Games and Asian Para Games respectively, reflecting the growing strength and ambition of Indian sport. However, doping remained a serious concern, requiring sustained efforts in education, prevention, testing and enforcement. “During 2025–26, the National Anti-Doping Agency of India conducted over 7,000 tests and more than 350 education and awareness sessions, reaching 27,000 participants,” Dr. Mandaviya added.
“Supplement testing facilities at National Forensic Sciences University, Gandhinagar and National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, Hyderabad further help prevent cases of inadvertent doping, while investigations within NADA would be strengthened in line with global practices. The National Anti-Doping Act came into force this year and the government is also preparing to bring provisions for the criminalisation of doping-related activities before Parliament,” he said.
Hon’ble Education Minister Pralhad Joshi said the MoU would help address the longstanding gap between education and sports. He also observed that students who performed well academically did not always participate in sports, and emphasised the need to strengthen grassroots opportunities and build better pathways for young athletes.
“This MoU is an important step towards strengthening the connection between education and sports, which has been missing for a long time. Through this initiative, we are working to ensure that sports values become an integral part of every child’s educational experience,” Shri Joshi said. “I’m very happy that children are now being educated about clean sport and the values associated with it. The values being introduced through this toolkit must spread beyond classrooms and reach every section of society. By integrating sports values into education, we can help nurture responsible citizens and build a culture of fairness and integrity from an early age.”
Dr. Tim Curtis described the MoU as a new chapter in UNESCO’s partnership with India, with the potential to reach millions of young people and offer a model that other countries could learn from. “Every child in the classroom can learn what it means to play by the rules. Through this toolkit, we are bringing three fundamental values into education and sport: respect, integrity and fairness,” the Australian said.
“The toolkit offers ideas and practical resources, but teachers are the ones who bring these values to life. We need to look at what happens in the schoolyard and how children treat one another in everyday situations. The real test of these values is whether children play fairly even when nobody is watching. That is the kind of integrity we want to nurture from an early age,” Dr. Curtis added.

title: Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana Strengthens India’s Commitment to Dignified Ageing
subtitle: Central Government Releases ₹ 77.98 Crore In Grant-In-Aid To 755 Projects Under The Integrated Programme For Senior Citizens For The Quarter Ending 30 September 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Reflecting the Central Government’s continued commitment to senior citizens, an amount of ₹ 77.98 Crore has been released as Grant-In-Aid to 755 projects under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) component of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), for the quarter ending 30 September 2026 in the financial year 2026–27.
AVYAY is one of the flagship schemes of the Ministry of Social Justice And Empowerment that embodies the principles of
‘Ageing with Dignity’
and
‘Ageing in Place’
, recognising the importance of ensuring that older persons can live with respect, security and independence.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the support is aimed at strengthening service delivery and welfare interventions for senior citizens through assisted institutional care and related facilities.
He said the country is witnessing a significant demographic transition, highlighting the growing need for comprehensive and accessible support systems for senior citizens. He added that with India’s senior citizen population projected to reach 23 crore by 2036, the need for a comprehensive and responsive support system is becoming increasingly important. He said AVYAY seeks to address this emerging demographic challenge by strengthening institutional mechanisms and encouraging community participation, enabling older persons to lead dignified, secure and meaningful lives.
According to Census 2011, India had 10.38 crore people aged 60 years and above, comprising 5.11 Crore Males And 5.27 Crore Females, and the  Longitudinal Ageing Study in India (LASI) highlights functional limitations among a substantial proportion of older persons, underscoring the need for reliable care, healthcare services and community-based support, he said.
The Official said increasing urbanisation, migration and the growth of nuclear households are also changing traditional family support structures, making institutional and community-based care increasingly important for the well-being of senior citizens.
He informed that the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) launched in 2021, and subsumed and expanded the earlier National Action Plan for Senior Citizens (NAPSrC), bringing multiple interventions for senior citizens under a unified umbrella scheme.
The Official further said the Scheme aims to provide functional support and promote active ageing by facilitating shelter, food, healthcare and recreational services, while strengthening the capacities of governments, non-governmental organisations, local bodies and communities to support older persons.
The Official noted that under AVAY, the spirit and emotions attached to ageing with dignity focuses on providing respectful and empowering care that recognises the lifelong contributions of senior citizens. Ageing in place promotes an environment in which older persons can continue living safely in their own homes and communities, supported by suitable home modifications and specialised community-based services wherever required, he added.
The Ministry official elaborated that through AVYAY, the Government continues to strengthen the ecosystem of care and support for senior citizens by combining institutional assistance, state-level planning and district-level monitoring. He said the scheme reflects a holistic approach to ageing that places the dignity, well-being, independence and social inclusion of older persons at its centre.
It is pertinent to mention that the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, through the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, serves as the nodal authority for AVYA, to undertake policy formulation, financial support, monitoring and overall implementation of the scheme.
The State and Union Territory Governments play an important role through the State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) component. Under this framework, States and UTs prepare and implement action plans tailored to their respective requirements for senior citizen welfare, with financial support from the Ministry for the formulation and implementation of these plans.
At the district level, District Committees chaired by the District Collector or District Magistrate play a key role in the selection of eligible indigent beneficiaries and the monitoring of senior citizen homes. This decentralised framework supports the identification of local needs and strengthens oversight of welfare services at the grassroots level.

title: Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme
subtitle: Building a Globally Competitive Sports Manufacturing Ecosystem
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme on 28 October 2026 with an outlay of
₹
1,856.67 crore for FY 2026-27 to FY 2033-34. Dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones will bring manufacturers, suppliers, testing facilities and design centres together in one place. Support for anchor investment and turnover-linked production, with a combined outlay of
₹
1,130 crore, will draw new investment and raise production. A further
₹
105 crore will help manufacturers obtain and renew certification from International Sports Federations. Centres of Excellence, start-up support, skilling and export promotion complete a scheme that aims to make India a global hub for high-quality sports goods.
Introduction
India’s sporting ambitions are creating opportunities that extend from playgrounds and training centres to manufacturing and enterprise. Initiatives such as
Khelo India
and
Khelo Bharat Niti 2025
are strengthening participation, talent development and sports infrastructure. A strong sports goods industry can support this vision by supplying quality equipment while creating opportunities for skills, employment and exports.
India’s sports goods manufacturing base draws on established clusters such as
Jalandhar (Punjab) and Meerut (Uttar Pradesh)
, skilled workers and a network of entrepreneurial MSMEs. Small and micro enterprises account for nearly
90% of production
, making the sector an important avenue for local enterprise and employment. The global sports equipment market, valued at approximately
US$140 billion in 2024
, is projected to reach around
US$283 billion by 2036
, offering substantial opportunities for Indian manufacturers to expand their presence.
To build on these strengths, the Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the
Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme
, with a total outlay of
₹
1,856.67 crore
for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2033-34
. Announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, the scheme brings together support for investment, technology, innovation, skills and market development to position India as a globally competitive hub for the design, development and manufacture of sports goods. The Budget Speech 2026-27 noted that “India has the potential to emerge as a global hub for high quality, affordable sports goods.”
Key Interventions under the Scheme
The scheme provides support across the sports goods manufacturing value chain, from infrastructure and investment to research, skills, certification and market development. It has two parts: incentives that support manufacturing and interventions that build the wider ecosystem.
Developing integrated manufacturing zones: The integrated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs)
will bring together manufacturers, suppliers, testing facilities, design and prototyping centres, and ancillary enterprises. Developed through convergence with the
BHAVYA Scheme and NICDC Industrial Parks
, these zones will strengthen industry linkages and improve manufacturing efficiency. There may be f
our such integrated zones, each covering more than 300 acres.
Attracting investment and expanding production:
Two components, with a
combined outlay of ₹
1,130 crore
, will support manufacturing growth.
Anchor Investment Support
will provide
20% capital expenditure support to anchor investors investing at least ₹
100 crore
, encouraging leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs).
Turnover Linked Support
will offer
incentives of up to 15% to manufacturers investing ₹
10 crore or more
, encouraging higher production and capacity expansion.
Upgrading existing clusters and supporting MSMEs:
Existing sports goods manufacturing clusters will receive support for upgrading
common facilities and shared infrastructure through cost-sharing with States
, helping smaller enterprises strengthen their manufacturing capabilities.
Supporting international certification:
An outlay of
₹
105 crore
will help manufacturers obtain and renew certifications from International Sports Federations. Support will cover
70% of first-time certification costs and 50% of renewal costs
, promoting internationally accepted quality and performance standards and facilitating global market access.
Advancing research and start-up innovation: Centres of Excellence
in premier educational and research institutions will support research in sports equipment, material sciences, protective gear and advanced manufacturing technologies. Research co-funding will be encouraged through convergence with the
Anusandhan National Research Foundation
.
DPIIT-registered sports start-ups will be eligible for grants of up to ₹
20 lakh
. Aligned with
Startup India
, this support will facilitate the development, testing, validation and commercialisation of new technologies, processes and products.
Developing industry-aligned skills:
Skill development initiatives will be implemented in collaboration with the
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
and relevant industry stakeholders to meet evolving workforce requirements.
Promoting Indian sports goods globally:
An
India Sports Expo and a Brand India campaign
, alongside branding, outreach and market development initiatives drawing on the
Export Promotion Mission
, will strengthen the visibility of Indian sports goods and support wider access to international markets.
Strengthening India’s Sports Goods Manufacturing Base
India’s Sports Goods Industry Today
India’s sports goods industry combines established manufacturing skills with a broad network of small enterprises. Its strengths extend beyond individual products to clusters of manufacturers, suppliers and household units serving domestic and international buyers.
An established manufacturing network:
Jalandhar and Meerut together comprise
over 250 exporting units, more than 1,000 domestic-market units, over 4,000 micro enterprises and nearly 20,000 household units
. Other centres include Ludhiana for bicycles and Delhi and Mumbai for sports accessories and apparel.
Strong MSME participation:
Nearly
90% of production
is undertaken by small and micro enterprises. This makes growth in sports manufacturing closely connected with entrepreneurship, local livelihoods and employment.
Products with an international presence:
India manufactures cricket bats, protective gear, inflatable balls, and gym and athletic training equipment. The
United Kingdom, United States and Australia together receive over half of India’s sports equipment exports
, providing established connections with major overseas markets.
Areas of strength:
India-based brands and manufacturers together account for about 75 to 80% of the global cricket bat market, and India holds an estimated 30 to 35% of the cricket helmet market.
Opportunities across related industries:
Sports equipment production draws on capabilities in rubber, polymers, composites, wood and metals. Shared materials, machinery and skills create opportunities to diversify products and strengthen supplier networks across industries.
Scope to serve domestic and global demand:
India’s domestic sports goods market is estimated at
US$2.5 billion
, including approximately
US$0.5 billion in equipment
. Globally, equipment exports reached around
US$52 billion in 2024
, offering opportunities to expand beyond India’s existing equipment exports of
US$275 million
.
Significant long-term potential:
India’s sports equipment exports could reach approximately
US$8.1 billion by 2036
, potentially generating around
54 lakh additional direct and indirect jobs
.
A decade of major events:
the Los Angeles Olympics 2028, the Commonwealth Games 2030 in Ahmedabad, the Brisbane Olympics 2032 and India’s planned bid for the 2036 Olympic Games create a decade of demand for sports equipment.
Together, these strengths provide a foundation for expanding production, developing higher-value equipment and building a greater international presence. Technology, testing, certification and industry partnerships can help translate this potential into manufacturing growth.
Building on These Strengths through the New Scheme
The Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme brings together support across the manufacturing value chain. Its interventions address the following priorities:
Stronger Domestic Manufacturing:
Integrated manufacturing zones and investment and production support will encourage capacity expansion, strengthen supplier networks, increase domestic value addition and reduce import dependence.
Growth of MSMEs:
Upgradation of existing clusters, common facilities and shared infrastructure will support smaller enterprises.
Better Quality and Innovation:
Research centres, technology development, start-up support and international certification will strengthen product development and quality.
Skills and Employment:
Training aligned with industry requirements will help develop a skilled workforce and support employment across the value chain.
Greater Global Competitiveness:
Branding, outreach and market development will help Indian sports goods reach international buyers.
Support for India’s Sporting Ambitions:
High-quality, internationally certified equipment will support the sports sector and athlete development programmes, complementing Khelo India and Fit India.
Convergence with National Schemes and Initiatives
The scheme builds on existing national initiatives to connect manufacturing infrastructure with research, skills and export opportunities. It also supports the wider goal of strengthening India’s sporting ecosystem.
Manufacturing Infrastructure
BHAVYA:
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojna provides for
100 plug-and-play industrial parks
with an allocation of
₹
33,660 crore
. Facilities such as ready-built factory sheds, testing laboratories and warehousing provide the infrastructure needed by manufacturers. The scheme’s Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones will be developed through convergence with infrastructure under the BHAVYA Scheme.
National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation Limited (NICDC):
NICDC helps develop industrial cities with land, roads, power, water and transport links for manufacturers. Its industrial corridor programme covers
20 industrial smart cities across 13 States
, with
four completed as of September 2026
. The sports goods scheme will use infrastructure in NICDC Industrial Parks to develop manufacturing zones that bring manufacturers, suppliers and supporting facilities together.
Research and Innovation
Anusandhan National Research Foundation:
ANRF supports research and collaboration between educational institutions, research organisations and industry. Convergence with ANRF will encourage R&D in the sports goods sector, alongside the scheme’s support for Centres of Excellence working on equipment, materials, protective gear and manufacturing technologies.
Startup India:
Startup India supports new enterprises through seed funding, investment and credit guarantees, helping ideas progress into viable businesses. As of
31 March 2026
, India had over
2.23 lakh recognised start-ups
, which had generated more than
23.36 lakh direct jobs
. The sports goods scheme’s dedicated start-up support will align with this wider ecosystem to encourage innovation in equipment, materials and manufacturing processes, from development and testing to validation and commercialisation.
Export Promotion
Export Promotion Mission:
With an outlay of
₹
25,060 crore for 2025-26 to 2030-31
, the Mission brings together export finance, quality compliance, logistics and market-access support, particularly for MSMEs and first-time exporters. Its two components,
Niryat Protsahan
and
Niryat Disha
, help exporters access finance, meet international standards and connect with overseas buyers through trade fairs, buyer-seller meets and warehousing facilities. The sports goods scheme will draw on this wider framework for branding, outreach and market development, helping Indian manufacturers strengthen their international presence.
Sports Development
Khelo India and Fit India:
Khelo India supports participation, talent development, training and sports infrastructure, while Fit India promotes fitness and an active lifestyle. The manufacturing scheme will complement these efforts by strengthening the capacity to produce high-quality, internationally certified sports goods for India’s sports sector and athlete development programmes.
Khelo India Scheme
Launched in 2017:
brought the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan, the Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme and the National Sports Talent Search Scheme into one framework for sports development.
Five pillars:
training centres to identify talent; capacity building for coaches and support staff; sports science and technology; competitions and leagues; and sports infrastructure.
Reach as of July 2026:
349 sports infrastructure projects approved with an investment of ₹3,176 crore; 1,067 Khelo India Centres; 267 academies supported; and 2,745 Khelo India Athletes supported with coaching, equipment, medical care and a monthly allowance.
Policy Alignment
Khelo Bharat Niti 2025:
The policy recognises sport as a driver of economic growth, including through entrepreneurship, investment and sports start-ups. The manufacturing scheme supports this approach by connecting sporting development with opportunities for production, innovation, employment and exports.
Khelo Bharat Niti 2025
National sports policy:
uses sport for nation-building, economic growth and social inclusion, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Grassroots to elite:
early identification and nurturing of talent, competitive leagues, and infrastructure in rural and urban areas.
Sport for all:
sport in the school curriculum under the National Education Policy 2020, and wider participation of women, marginalised groups, tribal communities and persons with disabilities.
Production Linked Incentive Schemes: Supporting Manufacturing Growth
The
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes
reward increases in production and sales across
14 sectors
, encouraging investment and competitive manufacturing.
As of
June 2026
, these schemes had:
· Attracted
₹
2.6 lakh crore in investment
.
· Generated
₹
23.8 lakh crore in production and sales
.
· Supported
over
₹
15.5 lakh crore in exports
.
· Created
14.6 lakh jobs
.
Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047:
By expanding domestic manufacturing, increasing value addition and reducing import dependence, the scheme supports Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat. Its focus on investment, employment and exports also contributes to the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
Towards a Global Hub for Sports Goods
The scheme is expected to position India as a globally competitive hub for the design, development and manufacture of sports goods. By strengthening manufacturing, promoting innovation and widening access to global markets, it will create new opportunities for growth, employment and exports, and support India’s aspiration to emerge as a leading sporting nation.

title: Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana
subtitle: Strengthening Governance at the Grassroots
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                28 OCT 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana is a
Centrally Sponsored Scheme
approved for 2026-27 to 2030-31, with a total outlay of
₹
7,395.55 crore
. It covers
all States and Union Territories
, including eligible traditional rural local government institutions. The scheme seeks to
strengthen Gram Panchayats
as centres of integrated and participatory development planning. Annual targets include
2.55 lakh-plus gram development plans
and
2.55 lakh-plus online audit plans
. Each coordinated awareness intervention will aim to reach
at least one crore citizens
. Digital integration, capacity building and financial accountability are key mechanisms planned for improving grassroots governance.
The Blueprint for Viksit Gram Swaraj
The Union Cabinet, on 28 October, 2026, has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana. It is a
Centrally Sponsored Scheme
for
transforming rural local governance
. The initiative aligns grassroots development with the national vision of
Viksit Bharat
. It aims to
transform Panchayats
into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government.
The PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana at a Glance
Implementation Period
2026-27 to 2030-31
Total Financial Outlay
₹7,395.55 crore
Central Government Share
₹4,869.48 crore
State Government Share
₹2,526.07 crore
Direct Beneficiaries
Around 32 lakh elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders.
Institutional Coverage
Over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies.
Geographical Coverage
All States and Union Territories, including traditional rural local government institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist.
Funding the Transformation
PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana has a total outlay of
₹
7,395.55 crore
. The Central Government will contribute
₹
4,869.48 crore
. State Governments will contribute
₹
2,526.07 crore
. The scheme period coincides with the
Sixteenth Finance Commission period
. The Commission has recommended approximately
₹
4.35 lakh crore
in
grants
for Rural Local Bodies during 2026-27 to 2030-31. This scheme will help Panchayats use these resources more effectively. It will
connect national priorities, government schemes, available funds, and local aspirations
.
Six Pillars of Grassroots Transformation
PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana focuses on
six holistic pillars
that will strengthen identification of local constraints, improve local planning and governance capabilities, promote digital integration, and ensure transparent resource utilisation at the grassroots level.
1.
Gram Panchayats as Hubs of Local Governance
: PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana places Gram Panchayats at the
centre of local development planning
. Panchayats will coordinate village priorities, government interventions, and available resources. This approach will connect national development goals with rural communities’ needs and aspirations.
2.
Holistic Planning at Gram Panchayat Level
: The scheme will bring Central and State departmental planning processes onto a common digital platform. This will support holistic
Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs)
. The integrated approach will help departments identify gaps, align interventions, and use available resources effectively. Existing departmental arrangements for delivering individual schemes will continue.
3.
Digital Governance
: Building on
eGramSwaraj
and existing e-Panchayat systems, PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will consolidate information on a
common digital platform
. The platform will include government schemes, beneficiaries, benefits, community assets, and available resources. This will help Panchayats identify development gaps and improve planning, coordination, and monitoring. This platform will also help in knowledge sharing among Gram Panchayats of different States.
eGramSwaraj
eGramSwaraj, launched in 2020, is a work-based comprehensive application for Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). It encompasses
all aspects of Panchayat functioning
, i.e., planning, budgeting, accounting, monitoring, asset management etc.
on a single digital platform
including online payments. eGramSwaraj has been
integrated with various government digital platforms
, including the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) for online payments and financial management, Government e-Marketplace (GeM) for procurement, BHASHINI for multilingual AI-enabled services, BSNL for BharatNet connectivity monitoring and the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for weather-related information.
4.
Connecting National Priorities with Local Needs
: The scheme will use existing training, digital, and outreach platforms to explain government initiatives in accessible language. Gram Sabhas and Panchayat forums will encourage informed community discussions, thereby, encouraging
Jan Bhagidari
.
PANCHAM
will support this effort through AI-enabled, multilingual, and two-way communication in
17 Indian languages
. These platforms will help connect national priorities with local needs and village development goals.
PANCHAM - Panchayat Assistance and Messaging Chatbot
Launched in January 2026, PANCHAM is a
WhatsApp-based tool
for direct, timely, and two-way
digital interaction
with Panchayat Elected Representatives, officials, and citizens. PANCHAM enables easy access to scheme updates, training content, surveys and Panchayat service information,
strengthening transparent and effective service delivery
at the grassroots.
5.
Capacity Building to put the Approach into Practice
: PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will strengthen the capabilities of elected representatives and Panchayat functionaries. This will be conducted through Integrated Government Online Training and the National Academy for Capacity Building of Civil Services. Both
specialized
(for example, preparing engineering estimate) and
general training
would be imparted to local representatives.
Capacity building
will support the effective use of digital platforms, interpretation of scheme and resource information, holistic planning, and communication with citizens. These capabilities will help Panchayats translate local discussions into development plans and follow-up action.
6.
Transparent and Efficient Utilization of Available Resources
: The scheme will strengthen Panchayats’ capacity to utilise Finance Commission grants and other funds effectively. It will also support
Own Source Revenue (OSR) mobilisation.
Online accounting, auditing and public disclosure will improve financial accountability. These measures will promote transparent resource utilisation and support financially self-reliant Panchayats.
Turning the Vision into Measurable Outcomes
PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana sets
annual targets
for planning, citizen awareness, capacity building and financial accountability:
The scheme will support the preparation of more than2.55 lakh GPDPs annually on the eGramSwaraj Portal.
These plans will integrate village priorities, Central and State departmental interventions, and available resources. Coordinated awareness campaigns will improve public understanding of government schemes and national initiatives.
At least 1 crore citizens are targeted to be reached per awareness-generation episode.
Digital platforms, outreach activities, Gram Sabhas and Panchayat forums will support citizen engagement. These awareness-generation episodes will aim to improve understanding of relevant Government schemes and national initiatives, encouraging
informed discussion of their local implications
.
Around 32 lakh governance stakeholders will be supported annually.
These include elected representatives, Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, who will receive capacity building and digital handholding. These interventions will strengthen planning, citizen communication, resource management and progress towards locally relevant
Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
The scheme will support at least 2.55 lakh online audit plans annually.
Corresponding audits are expected to be completed on time through
AuditOnline
. Improved accounting and public disclosure will strengthen accountability for available funds.
AuditOnline
The AuditOnline application was launched in 2020 for carrying out
online audits of Panchayati Raj accounts
for further strengthening the financial management and transparency of the Panchayats. This application is configurable as per every States' Audit Act/Rules.
How the Scheme Will Be Implemented
PM Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana will operate through existing government institutions and systems. State Governments and Union Territory Administrations will submit
Annual Action Plans
. These will specify activities, priorities and requirements under the scheme. The designated
Central Empowered Committee
will appraise and approve these plans. The process will follow applicable procedures and norms. The Central Government and State/UT administrations will undertake activities within their respective responsibilities. Coordination will support implementation across administrative levels. Technical assistance, monitoring, and review will support implementation. Existing institutional, digital, capacity-building, and communication systems will facilitate grassroots delivery.
The scheme does not provide for the creation of permanent posts. However, it has a provision to engage contractual personnel based on need at the State, District and Block levels. These personnel will provide technical support and help achieve the scheme’s objectives.
Empowering Villages Through Stronger Local Governance
The Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana seeks to
make rural governance more effective and accountable
. It brings planning, digital systems, community participation, and financial management together. The scheme responds to the need for stronger grassroots institutions as rural development resources and national initiatives expand. It aims to make local governance more coordinated, transparent, and responsive to community priorities. This approach seeks to strengthen grassroots institutions as key drivers of inclusive rural development, contributing to the broader vision of
Viksit Bharat
.

content:
Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme
Maritime transport is a cornerstone of global trade, with shipping containers playing a vital role in the seamless movement of goods across borders. As of February 2026, India’s maritime sector facilitated
95%
of the country’s trade by volume and
70%
by value. Beyond its role in trade, the sector contributes
4-5% to India’s GDP
.
As India strengthens its position in global manufacturing and international commerce, the demand for containerised cargo movement continues to grow, underscoring the need to build domestic container manufacturing capabilities. To amplify this, the Union Cabinet has approved the
Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme (CMPS)
with budgetary outlay of ₹
10,000 crore up to FY 2039-40
.
What are Containers?
Shipping containers are standardized steel freight containers that transport cargo across ships, railways and road vehicles without unloading and repacking the goods during transit. Built as per ISO (International Organization for Standardization) specifications, they enable seamless intermodal transport and efficient global trade. The most common sizes are 20-foot and 40-foot containers, measured in Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), the standard unit used to measure container capacity.
Building India’s Container Manufacturing Ecosystem
CMPS supports the Government's initiatives under Make in India, Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 and multimodal logistics development, contributing to India's long-term maritime and trade ambitions-
DID YOU KNOW?
As per the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD),
~80%
of global merchandise trade by volume is transported by sea.
It aims to
establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem
by promoting domestic manufacturing and encouraging investment across the value chain.
The initiative seeks to
reduce import dependence
and
strengthen supply-chain resilience.
It also
supports new manufacturing facilities
and
expands existing container manufacturing units.
Components under CMPS
The scheme provides assistance through major components:
investment support, operational expenditure, and testing and certification.
Interest Subvention Assistance (ISA)
With a financial outlay of
₹859 crore
, ISA provides a 3% per annum interest subvention on eligible term loans (capital loans) availed by container manufacturers to set up
greenfield facilities and brownfield expansion
of existing manufacturing capacity. To qualify for this support, projects must meet the following criteria:
Greenfield and Brownfield Facilities
A greenfield project involves building a completely
new asset,
while a brownfield project involves upgrading, renovating, or repurposing an
existing asset.
Greenfield facilities must have an annual capacity of at least
1,00,000 TEUs;
Brownfield expansions must add at least
25,000 TEUs
of annual capacity to be
commissioned within three years
of in-principle approval, and
comply with global container standards.
Operational Expenditure Assistance (OEA)
The component provides a financial outlay of
₹8,891 crore
to support containers manufactured as per global shipping standards and sold by eligible manufacturers. The assistance is intended to bridge the cost gap and improve the competitiveness of domestically manufactured containers.
Operational Expenditure Assistance (OEA) by Container Type
Container Type
Assistance Value (per container)
20 ft Container
₹49,500
40 ft Container
₹86,625
20 ft Specialised Container
₹37,125-₹74,250
To avail support, manufacturers must meet a
minimum local-content requirement of 70%
through FY 2031-32. These criteria will further
rise to 90%
from FY 2032-33 to strengthen the domestic supply chain.
Testing and certification assistance
A financial outlay of
₹150
crore
has been allocated to support the setting up of common facilities such as Dynamic longitudinal impact.
Expected Outcomes and Wider Economic Impact
The scheme aims to expand domestic container production while strengthening India’s export potential, supply chains and related industries.
Expanded manufacturing capacity:
Annual domestic container manufacturing capacity is expected to increase by around ten-fold, up to
7.5 lakh TEUs
.
Export potential:
It will help build a
globally competitive container manufacturing base
and help India strengthen its potential to position itself as a
global export hub
for quality shipping containers.
Supply-chain resilience:
The resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains is expected to strengthen.
Employment generation:
It aims to generate an estimated
3,000 direct jobs
and
over 50,000 indirect jobs.
Support for ancillary industries:
The Scheme is also expected to benefit industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints.
Strengthening India’s Maritime Ecosystem
In addition to CMPS, various other measures have been undertaken to build an integrated, domestically anchored logistics ecosystem.
Establishment of the Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL)
To build and support an integrated container ecosystem anchored in India, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed in February 2026 to establish the
Bharat Container Shipping Line (BCSL).
The agreement brings together the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI), Container Corporation of India (CONCOR), Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA), V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority (VOCPA), Chennai Port Authority and Sagarmala Finance Corporation Limited (SMFCL), under the aegis of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.
The MoU will
establish a self-reliant container shipping ecosystem
linking JNPA, VOCPA and Chennai ports with inland markets. It aims to improve end-to-end logistics, stabilise freight costs and strengthen India’s trade competitiveness.
Broader Support for the Maritime Sector
Several complementary government initiatives are also strengthening India’s maritime sector.
Area of Support
Key Measures and Initiatives
Legislative Support
Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, the Coastal Shipping Act, 2025 and the Indian Ports Act, 2025
Digital Support for Ease of Doing Business
One Nation One Port Process (ONOP), the Maritime Single Window and e-Samudra
Integrated Logistics Network
PM Gati Shakti, The National Logistics Policy (NLP), The Sagarmala Programme
Conclusion
CMPS
is set to
strengthen India’s maritime manufacturing capabilities
, enhance supply-chain resilience and create employment opportunities, while reducing import dependence. Aligned with broader maritime reforms, the scheme advances India’s ambition to
emerge as a globally competitive maritime manufacturing and logistics hub.
